title: ProjectSettings: resolve feature-tag ('.web') setting overrides via get_setting_with_override
description:
[audit-key: project-settings-runtime-honoring-and-script-api/projectsettings-feature-override] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]
[verify-note: ADJUSTED: Finding substance CONFIRMED but status should be MISSING, not PARTIAL. Every resolution behavior is absent: get_setting_with_override = 0 hits; custom_features/feature_override = 0 runtime hits; OS.has_feature is not implemented (no has_feature in interpreter OS static call_os_static at in]

GODOT: A setting key suffixed with a feature tag (e.g. display/window/size/viewport_width.web=800) overrides the base key when OS.has_feature("web") is true. get_setting_with_override(name) applies the active OS feature tags; get_setting_with_override_and_custom_features takes an explicit tag list (upstream core/config/project_settings.cpp).

PATINA: No override resolution. GodotProjectFile stores .web keys verbatim (project.rs:32) and ProjectConfig reads only base keys (project.rs:172-215); the browser target therefore silently ignores web-specific overrides. Only the editor's project generator touches custom features (project_manager.rs:624).

APPROACH: Add override resolution to the settings store used at boot: when reading key K, if K.<feature> exists for any active OS feature tag (query gdplatform feature tags - 'web','wasm32', etc.), return that value. Expose get_setting_with_override(name) and get_setting_with_override_and_custom_features(name,features) on the store, and have the boot honoring paths (physics/display) resolve through it. WIRING: project.godot with a .web override -> web-tagged boot -> overridden value applied.
acceptance_criteria: Given project.godot with display/window/size/viewport_width=1152 and display/window/size/viewport_width.web=800, resolving through the settings store with feature tag 'web' active returns 800 (and 1152 without it); get_setting_with_override_and_custom_features(name,["web"]) returns 800. Proven via the store's public API exercised through a boot-config test. (test: project_settings_feature_override)

title: ProjectSettings: honor display/window size + default clear color (+ max_fps) from project.godot at boot
description:
[audit-key: project-settings-runtime-honoring-and-script-api/projectsettings-display-rendering-honor] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

GODOT: The runtime configures the root Window/viewport size from display/window/size/viewport_width/height, the frame cap from application/run/max_fps, and the default background from rendering/environment/defaults/default_clear_color at startup.

PATINA: None honored. BootConfig hardcodes 1152x648 (bootstrap.rs:157) with window_size() only used in tests; the 2D renderer clear color defaults to the viewport/Color::BLACK (renderer.rs:546, wgpu_backend.rs:107) rather than the project's default_clear_color (0 grep hits); max_fps has no consumer. ProjectConfig already carries viewport_width/height (project.rs) so the parse exists but is dropped.

APPROACH: In patina-runner boot, populate BootConfig/render viewport dims from ProjectConfig.viewport_width/height, read rendering/environment/defaults/default_clear_color (extend ProjectConfig or read via the settings store) and pass it as the framebuffer/wgpu clear color, and thread application/run/max_fps into the MainLoop frame cap. (Window content-scale/stretch APPLICATION is a Viewport pipeline concern tracked by scene-tree/web-runtime; this bead covers reading+applying size, clear color, and fps.) WIRING: project.godot -> render viewport dims + clear color observable in the runner's rendered output/JSON.
acceptance_criteria: Booting the runner on a project whose project.godot sets display/window/size/viewport_width=800, viewport_height=600 and rendering/environment/defaults/default_clear_color=Color(0.1,0.2,0.3,1) produces a render target of 800x600 whose cleared background pixel equals that color - via the boot path, not manual overrides. (test: project_display_settings_honored)

title: Notifications: deliver Object::notification -> _notification(int) virtual to attached GDScripts
description:
[audit-key: notification-virtual-delivery-to-gdscript/notification_virtual_delivery] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: every notification an object receives is delivered to its script's `_notification(int what)` virtual, for ALL scripts in the inheritance chain that override it (core/object/object.cpp:1010-1048 -> ScriptInstance::notification; modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:1917 GDScriptInstance::notification looks up the `_notification` member function and calls it with `what`). This is how PREDELETE/POSTINITIALIZE (Object) and ENTER_TREE/READY/EXIT_TREE/PAUSED/UNPAUSED/PROCESS/PHYSICS_PROCESS (Node) and all app/window notifications reach user code. Patina current state: the `ScriptInstance` trait (crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs:129) has no `notification` method, and every notification sink only appends to an internal `Vec<Notification>` log (crates/gdscene/src/node.rs:426 receive_notification; crates/gdobject/src/object.rs:211 record_notification). Scripts only ever receive the five NAMED lifecycle callbacks via crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:1410 call_script_with_access (:1465-1491). No `_notification` is ever called on a script for any code, so save-on-quit, focus-pause, re-localize, etc. are impossible. Implementation approach: (1) add `fn notification(&mut self, what: i64, reversed: bool)` to the `ScriptInstance` trait (bindings.rs) with a default no-op; (2) implement it on `GDScriptNodeInstance` (crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs) to call the `_notification` GDScript method (if defined) with `[Variant::Int(what)]` via the existing interpreter call path, wrapped in the same SceneTreeAccessor set_scene_access/clear_scene_access frame used by call_script_with_access; (3) add a `SceneTree::notify_script(node_id, what)` helper and call it from EVERY existing notification site — crates/gdscene/src/lifecycle.rs:41/54/73 (ENTER_TREE/READY/EXIT_TREE), crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:236 (PAUSED/UNPAUSED), crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:1536-1634 (PROCESS/PHYSICS_PROCESS/INTERNAL_*), and :1781 (PREDELETE) — additively alongside the existing named dispatch and the node log push. Wiring requirement: the call path Node notification -> SceneTree::notify_script -> GDScriptNodeInstance::notification -> interpreter `_notification(what)` must exist end-to-end and be driven by the MainLoop tick / LifecycleManager, not only by tests. Depends on the companion bead that adds the NOTIFICATION_* constants to the interpreter (same group_key) so `what` comparisons resolve.
acceptance_criteria: A scene-loaded node with a GDScript that overrides `func _notification(what)` and records each `what` observes, in order, NOTIFICATION_ENTER_TREE then NOTIFICATION_READY on enter, NOTIFICATION_PAUSED/UNPAUSED when MainLoop.set_paused toggles, NOTIFICATION_PROCESS each frame, and NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE on queue_free — with values matching Godot (10,13,14/15,17,1). Prove via an integration test that loads a .tscn/attaches a script, runs LifecycleManager::enter_tree + a MainLoop frame + set_paused, and asserts the script's recorded notification list. (test: `notification_virtual_delivery`)

title: ProjectSettings: retain layer_names/{2d,3d}_{physics,render} keys and expose them via get_setting + inspector layer labels
description:
[audit-key: project-settings-runtime-honoring-and-script-api/projectsettings-layer-names] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

GODOT: project.godot may name each of the 32 collision/render layers (layer_names/2d_physics/layer_1="Player", etc.). These are readable via ProjectSettings.get_setting and drive the editor's layer-grid property editor tooltips (upstream core/config/project_settings.cpp default registration).

PATINA: No support - grep for layer_names yields 0 hits. The generic settings store must retain arbitrary keys (not just the handful ProjectConfig extracts) so layer_names/* survive, and get_setting must return them; the editor inspector layer grid should label bits from these keys.

APPROACH: Ensure the runtime settings store keeps ALL parsed project.godot keys (generic retention, not just the ProjectConfig allow-list), so layer_names/2d_physics/layer_N etc. are queryable via get_setting (depends on the script-API store from projectsettings-script-api). Wire the gdeditor collision/render layer property editor to read these names for labels/tooltips. WIRING: project.godot layer name -> get_setting result and editor layer-grid label.
acceptance_criteria: After loading a project whose project.godot sets layer_names/2d_physics/layer_1="Player", ProjectSettings.get_setting("layer_names/2d_physics/layer_1") returns "Player", and the editor's 2D physics layer grid labels bit 1 as "Player". (test: project_layer_names_exposed)

title: PrimitiveMesh3D: add Prism/Torus/Text/RibbonTrail/TubeTrail/Point + fix QuadMesh orientation
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/primitive-mesh3d] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]
[verify-note: ADJUSTED: Finding is REAL (PARTIAL/2 stay) but the evidence is materially wrong on TorusMesh — the finder searched only gdserver3d/primitive_mesh.rs and missed the ACTUAL editor render path (the acceptance target). REFUTED sub-claim 'TorusMesh missing': gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs:221 has a real Mesh3D::]

Godot provides 11 primitive meshes; Patina has 5 (Box/Sphere/Capsule/Cylinder/Plane, primitive_mesh.rs). Add PrismMesh (tapered box), TorusMesh (inner/outer radius, ring/radial segments), TextMesh (font-outline extrusion), RibbonTrailMesh + TubeTrailMesh (trail geometry with section counts + curve), and PointMesh (single point), matching Godot's vertex generation and default params (primitive_meshes.cpp; per-class XML). Also make QuadMesh a distinct XY-facing quad rather than an alias to the XZ PlaneMesh (render_server_3d.rs:574), respecting its `size`/`center_offset`/`orientation`. Register all primitive mesh classes in gdobject/class_db.rs so they construct from GDScript and .tscn sub_resources and appear in the Create-Mesh flow. Wiring: a .tscn with a TorusMesh sub-resource renders torus geometry (not a fallback cube/plane) in the editor viewport.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn whose MeshInstance3D uses a TorusMesh (and separately a PrismMesh) renders the correct silhouette in the editor viewport, and a QuadMesh renders facing +Z. Verified by (test: `primitive_meshes_torus_prism_quad_render`) asserting generated vertex bounds/orientation and non-empty rendered pixels.

title: MultiMesh3D: per-instance custom data (INSTANCE_CUSTOM) + visible_instance_count
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/multimesh3d] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot MultiMesh stores per-instance transform, optional color, and optional CUSTOM vec4 (set_instance_custom_data), and visible_instance_count limits rendering to the first N instances (multimesh.cpp; MultiMesh.xml). Patina's MultiMesh3D (multimesh.rs) has only transforms + colors + an unused use_custom_data flag and no visible count. Implementation: add a `custom_data: Vec<[f32;4]>` array (allocated when use_custom_data) with set/get accessors, a `visible_instance_count` field, include custom data in flatten_instance_data + the per-instance vertex attributes (wgpu_pipeline.rs instance buffer + WGSL INSTANCE_CUSTOM), and clamp the drawn instance range to visible_instance_count in renderer.rs/wgpu draw. Wiring: a .tscn MultiMeshInstance3D with visible_instance_count < instance_count renders only the visible subset, and custom-data feeds a shader.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn MultiMeshInstance3D with 10 instances and visible_instance_count=4 renders exactly 4 instances in the editor viewport, and per-instance custom data round-trips to the instance buffer. Verified by (test: `multimesh_visible_count_and_custom_data`).

title: Resources: wire .import remap resolution (source path → .godot/imported/*.ctex) into ResourceLoader
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/import-pipeline] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot's runtime never loads source PNG/WAV files; it reads the .import sidecar's [remap] path=res://.godot/imported/xxxx.ctex and loads that compiled artifact. Patina has the parser (importers.rs parse_import_file/load_import_file + ctex.rs) but nothing calls it during loading. Wire the ResourceLoader so that when loading res://asset.png it checks for asset.png.import, follows the [remap]/path to the .ctex/.oggvorbisstr artifact under .godot/imported/, and loads that (falling back to the source when no import exists, as the editor does).
acceptance_criteria: Loading res://icon.png where icon.png.import remaps to a .godot/imported/icon-*.ctex returns a texture whose pixels come from the .ctex artifact (not a re-decode of the source), verified by dimensions/format from the ctex header. (test: `resource_loader_follows_import_remap`)

title: Resources: wire uid:// resolution (uid_cache.bin + .uid sidecars) and expose the ResourceUID singleton
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/resource-uid] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot resolves uid://… references through a registry populated from res://.godot/uid_cache.bin and per-file .uid sidecars, letting scenes reference resources by UID even when paths move. Patina parses uid= attributes but never builds or consults such a registry, so uid-only ext_resource references and load("uid://…") cannot resolve. Populate gdresource::uid::UidRegistry at boot from uid_cache.bin/.uid sidecars, have the ResourceLoader consult it for uid:// paths, and expose the ResourceUID singleton (id_to_text/text_to_id/get_id_path/has_id) to GDScript.
acceptance_criteria: With a uid_cache.bin mapping uid://abc → res://sub.tscn, load("uid://abc").instantiate() loads the same scene as load("res://sub.tscn"), and ResourceUID.get_id_path(ResourceUID.text_to_id("uid://abc")) returns "res://sub.tscn". (test: `uid_resolves_to_path`)

title: DirAccess: add get_files/get_directories(+_at), copy, change_dir/get_current_dir, drives, space, and .import filtering
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/dir-access] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

The most common DirAccess usage in games/tools is DirAccess.get_files()/get_directories() and the static DirAccess.get_files_at(path); these plus copy/change_dir/get_current_dir are missing from gdcore/file_access.rs. Implement them (get_files returns non-dir entries with Godot's default .import/.godot + hidden filtering), add copy/change_dir/get_current_dir/get_drive*/get_space_left, and expose them through the interpreter DirAccess dispatch.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript calls DirAccess.get_files_at("res://assets") and receives the file names (excluding a sibling directory and any .import sidecar), and DirAccess.get_directories() on an opened dir lists only subdirectories. (test: `dir_access_get_files_and_directories`)

title: SceneTree: call_group/notify_group/set_group broadcasts + get_first_node_in_group/get_node_count_in_group/has_group
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/groups-broadcast] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot broadcasts to a group via call_group(group, method, ...args), call_group_flags(flags, ...), notify_group/notify_group_flags(what), and set_group/set_group_flags(property, value), honoring GROUP_CALL_REVERSE/DEFERRED/UNIQUE flags; plus get_first_node_in_group, get_node_count_in_group, and tree-level has_group (scene_tree.cpp). Patina only tracks membership (scene_tree.rs:864-918) with get_nodes_in_group. Implement the broadcasts over the existing group index: iterate members in tree order (reversible), invoke the named script method / set property / send notification, honoring DEFERRED by routing through the existing call_deferred queue (scene_tree.rs:1670) and UNIQUE de-duplication; add get_first_node_in_group/get_node_count_in_group/has_group. Expose to the GDScript bridge so get_tree().call_group('enemies','explode') reaches every member's script during a frame.
acceptance_criteria: call_group('g','take_damage',10) invokes take_damage on every scripted member during a MainLoop step; call_group_flags with DEFERRED defers until the frame's deferred flush; get_first_node_in_group returns the first member in tree order and get_node_count_in_group returns the member count. (test: scene_tree_group_broadcast)

title: Node: honor set_process/set_physics_process/is_processing toggles + request_ready
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/process-toggles] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

In Godot a node's _process/_physics_process run only while set_process(true)/set_physics_process(true) (default becomes enabled once the callback is defined), toggled at runtime independently of process_mode; set_process_input/unhandled_input gate input callbacks, and request_ready re-arms _ready on the next tree-enter (node.cpp process bitflags). Patina's Node has only process_priority/process_mode (node.rs:122-126) and dispatches to every scripted node passing should_process_node (scene_tree.rs:1498/1607) — a script calling set_process(false) still receives _process. Add per-node process / physics_process / internal-process enable flags (default true) to Node, gate process_all_scripts_* and process_frame_with_scripts on them, expose set_process/set_physics_process/is_processing/is_physics_processing/request_ready to the GDScript bridge, and clear/re-arm the ready flag via request_ready.
acceptance_criteria: A scripted node that calls set_process(false) in _ready receives no further _process callbacks across subsequent MainLoop steps while still receiving _physics_process; after request_ready() and re-entering the tree, _ready runs again. (test: node_process_toggles_gate_callbacks)

title: PackedScene/Node: editable instances, InstancePlaceholder, inherited scenes, duplicate() flags
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/instancing] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot instancing supports editable children (set_editable_instance exposes an instanced scene's internal nodes and persists overrides), InstancePlaceholder (set_scene_instance_load_placeholder defers instancing; InstancePlaceholder.create_instance() realizes it), inherited scenes (a .tscn whose root instances a base scene plus property/child diffs), and Node.duplicate(flags) copying signals/groups/scripts per DUPLICATE_* flags (packed_scene.cpp). Patina's packed_scene.rs handles none of these, and duplicate_subtree (scene_tree.rs:1177) copies only properties+groups+unique_name — no signals, no script, no flags. Implement editable-instance + load-placeholder flags on Node and honor them in add_packed_scene_to_tree (packed_scene.rs), add an InstancePlaceholder node with create_instance, support instances-of-instances/inherited roots during .tscn instancing, and give duplicate() a DuplicateFlags parameter that carries groups/signals/scripts.
acceptance_criteria: Instancing a scene that marks a child sub-scene editable exposes and applies overrides to its inner nodes; a placeholder-marked instance is an InstancePlaceholder until create_instance() is called; duplicate(DUPLICATE_GROUPS|DUPLICATE_SIGNALS) copies group membership and signal connections. (test: packed_scene_editable_placeholder_and_duplicate_flags)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
[IndigoBridge 2026-07-16] SCOPING ONLY — no code delivered this pass, deliberately. This is a 4-feature pack; I am NOT shipping a thin slice because a compile-clean partial auto-closes the whole bead and would mark 4 real parity gaps done. Handing off with a verified split.

VERIFIED STATE (greps 2026-07-16) — bead evidence is mostly right, with ONE correction:

- CORRECTION: the bead says "Patina's packed_scene.rs handles none of these". Not quite — `[editable path="..."]` IS already parsed and exposed: packed_scene.rs:115/124/230/516 collects `editable_instances`, and there's a public accessor `PackedScene::editable_instances()` (packed_scene.rs:657). It is PARSED BUT NOT HONORED: the only consumer is a test assertion (packed_scene.rs:3177). So the editable-instance work is "honor the already-parsed list during instancing", not "parse it".
- InstancePlaceholder / set_scene_instance_load_placeholder / load_placeholder: 0 hits. Genuinely missing.
- DuplicateFlags: 0 hits. Genuinely missing.
- duplicate_subtree (scene_tree.rs ~1177) copies properties + groups + unique_name only. No signals, no scripts, no flags. Confirmed.

STRUCTURAL BLOCKERS a future worker must know BEFORE starting (these are why this isn't a quick win):

1. DUPLICATE_SCRIPTS IS NOT IMPLEMENTABLE TODAY. `ScriptInstance` (gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs:135) is a trait object with NO clone/duplicate method, and scripts are held as `Box<dyn ScriptInstance>`. To copy a script on duplicate you must first add something like `fn clone_script(&self) -> Option<Box<dyn ScriptInstance>> { None }` as a DEFAULTED trait method (defaulted is mandatory — there are FIVE SceneAccess/ScriptInstance impls incl. test mocks), then implement it for GDScriptNodeInstance. That touches gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, which was exclusively reserved by GentleBadger (expires 02:22) at the time of this scoping.

2. SIGNALS CAN'T RIDE ON THE CURRENT API. `duplicate_subtree(&self, root) -> EngineResult<Vec<Node>>` returns DETACHED nodes, but signal connections live on the TREE: `SceneTree.signal_stores: HashMap<NodeId, SignalStore>` (scene_tree.rs:77). A detached Vec<Node> has nowhere to carry them. GOOD NEWS: `SignalStore` derives Clone (gdobject/src/signal.rs:282), so the copy itself is trivial ONCE the API can reach the tree. The fix is a new tree-level `duplicate_node(&mut self, root, flags) -> EngineResult<NodeId>` that inserts the clone AND clones signal_stores per old->new id mapping. Note `collect_subtree_top_down` and `duplicate_subtree` walk in the same deterministic order, so old_ids.zip(clones) gives the mapping without refactoring.

3. duplicate_subtree currently has NO production callers — only tests (packed_scene.rs:2154, :2180). So changing its behaviour is low-risk, but also means nothing in the engine actually duplicates nodes yet.

4. InstancePlaceholder needs a new node class REGISTERED in gdobject/src/class_db.rs, which was exclusively reserved by GreenBadger (expires 02:21) and GentleBadger (expires 02:16) at the time of this scoping. That file has been continuously contended for the last ~2h.

SUGGESTED SPLIT (4 beads):

a. Node.duplicate(flags) — the acceptance's third clause, and the best standalone win. Add DuplicateFlags (Godot: SIGNALS=1, GROUPS=2, SCRIPTS=4, USE_INSTANTIATION=8; default duplicate() = 1|2|4). Add tree-level `duplicate_node(root, flags) -> NodeId` that inserts the clone under the same parent, copies properties+unique_name always, groups only when GROUPS, and clones signal_stores when SIGNALS. Leave SCRIPTS unimplemented until (b) lands and say so. gdscene-only, no conflicted files. Test: duplicate with GROUPS|SIGNALS copies both; with neither copies neither.

b. DUPLICATE_SCRIPTS — add the defaulted `clone_script()` to ScriptInstance + implement for GDScriptNodeInstance. Needs interpreter.rs (contended).

c. Editable instances — honor the ALREADY-PARSED `PackedScene::editable_instances()` in add_packed_scene_to_tree: expose the named instance's inner nodes and apply overrides to them. Add a per-Node editable-instance flag. gdscene-only.

d. InstancePlaceholder + inherited scenes — new InstancePlaceholder node class + registration (needs class_db.rs, contended) + `set_scene_instance_load_placeholder` deferring instantiation + `create_instance()` realizing it; plus inherited-scene roots (a .tscn whose root instances a base scene plus diffs) during .tscn instancing.

RECOMMENDATION: (a) and (c) are clean gdscene-only beads a build-restricted worker can deliver. (b) and (d) are gated on the contended class_db.rs / interpreter.rs.

title: Shaders: execute sky/particles/fog/canvas_item shader types with per-stage built-ins
description:
[audit-key: shaders/shader-types-sky-particles-fog] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: each shader_type has its own stage functions and built-ins (shader_types.cpp) — sky shaders compute COLOR from EYEDIR/LIGHTn/radiance and drive the background; particles shaders run start()/process() writing TRANSFORM/VELOCITY/COLOR; fog shaders write DENSITY/ALBEDO/EMISSION into the volumetric fog; canvas_item shaders write COLOR from TEXTURE/SCREEN_UV in vertex/fragment/light. Patina current state: only Spatial(+a non-executed Sky enum) exists in gdserver3d; the wgpu sky is a fixed procedural shader (wgpu_pipeline.rs:330) not a user Sky ShaderMaterial; canvas_item fragment programs are parsed (gdserver2d) but never run by gdrender2d. Implementation approach: add ShaderType variants + per-stage built-in contexts for sky/particles/fog; execute a Sky ShaderMaterial to produce the background (feed from WorldEnvironment.sky), execute canvas_item fragment programs in gdrender2d's draw path, and hook particles shaders into the particle process step. Wiring requirement: a `shader_type sky` material on the environment changes background pixels, and a `shader_type canvas_item` material changes a Sprite2D's pixels, at runtime.
acceptance_criteria: A `shader_type sky` ShaderMaterial assigned to Environment/WorldEnvironment renders its computed COLOR as the viewport background, and a `shader_type canvas_item` ShaderMaterial on a CanvasItem alters its rendered pixels. (test: `sky_and_canvas_shader_types_render`)

comments.author: GentleBadger
comments.text: PARTIAL by GentleBadger (2026-07-16, uncommitted). Verify: '-p gdserver2d --lib shader' and '-p gdrender2d --lib draw' (both target-selector + module filter). NOT COMPILED by me (worker build policy) — eye-verified + reviewer pass. *** RE-SCOPE THIS BEAD: HALF IS ALREADY DONE. *** The claim 'canvas_item fragment programs are parsed (gdserver2d) but never run by gdrender2d' is FALSE — pat-u3l8c.45 already wired it: renderer.rs:304 canvas_item_set_material + renderer.rs:335 precomputes each item's fragment program (merging shader uniform defaults with material overrides), and draw::draw_texture_rect_shaded runs it PER-PIXEL. So the acceptance's second clause (canvas_item material alters a CanvasItem's pixels) appears ALREADY SATISFIED. Also stale: 'add ShaderType variants for sky/particles' — ShaderType::{Spatial,CanvasItem,Particles,Sky} all already exist (Fog does not). WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MISSING (now delivered): the sky STAGE could not be parsed or executed at all. Added parse_sky_body() (Godot's 'void sky()'), the EYEDIR built-in (FloatExpr::EyeDirComponent + Vec3Axis + FragmentContext.eyedir), and the real blocker — PER-COMPONENT COLOUR CONSTRUCTORS: parse_color_expr only understood vec4 with ALL-LITERAL components, so the canonical sky shader 'COLOR = vec3(EYEDIR.y, 0.0, 1.0)' parsed to NOTHING. Now vec3(...) (alpha 1.0, matching sky's vec3 COLOR) and non-literal vec4(...) evaluate per-component via ColorExpr::Components. This ALSO fixes canvas_item: 'COLOR = vec4(UV.x, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)' previously degraded silently to passthrough; it now works, including in generated WGSL. Both now have arms (Components -> real per-component WGSL; EyeDirComponent -> 0.0 there, since EYEDIR has no canvas_item counterpart, matching the CPU interpreter; pinned by a test). FragmentContext gained an eyedir field — only ONE full struct literal existed workspace-wide (gdrender2d/draw.rs:678), now spreads ..Default::default(). 7 new tests incl. a regression test that all-literal vec4 still parses to ColorExpr::Literal. KEEP OPEN — REMAINING: (1) SKY BACKGROUND WIRING (the acceptance's first clause): SkyMaterial in gdserver3d has Procedural/Panoramic/Physical but NO Shader variant, and nothing feeds sky COLOR into the viewport background (wgpu sky is still the fixed procedural shader). NB gdserver3d does NOT depend on gdserver2d, so this needs a new path dep or a caller that sees both crates. (2) particles + fog stages (no ShaderType::Fog). (3) the acceptance test sky_and_canvas_shader_types_render DOES NOT EXIST yet — do not trust a stale-recovery close (0-match filters exit 0). (4) sky built-ins beyond EYEDIR/TIME/uniforms (LIGHTn_*, SKY_COORDS, RADIANCE, AT_*_PASS) are not modelled.

title: Physics2D: wire RigidBody2D force/impulse/torque script API + angular dynamics
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-rigidbody-forces] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot ground truth (rigid_body_2d.cpp, RigidBody2D.xml): scripts drive rigid bodies via apply_central_impulse/apply_impulse(impulse,pos)/apply_central_force/apply_force(force,pos)/apply_torque/apply_torque_impulse/add_constant_force/add_constant_torque/set_axis_velocity, and _integrate_forces receives a PhysicsDirectBodyState2D. Positioned impulses/forces produce angular acceleration through the body's inertia; collisions impart spin. title: JavaScriptBridge: register a script-reachable singleton with real browser bindings
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web_js_bridge] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot's web export exposes the JavaScriptBridge singleton (javascript_bridge_singleton.cpp; JavaScriptBridge.xml) so GDScript can eval() JS, get_interface() globals, create_callback()/create_object(), download_buffer() to trigger a browser download, and force_fs_sync()/PWA update callbacks — the required interop surface for a browser engine. Patina has no such singleton (absent from class_db.rs and the interpreter singleton table, interpreter.rs:6224); gdplatform/web.rs's JsBridge is a fake unwired stub. Implementation: add a JavaScriptBridge singleton registered in gdobject/class_db.rs and dispatched by the interpreter alongside OS/Engine/Time, backed by real wasm-bindgen/js-sys bindings under cfg(target_arch=wasm32) (eval, get_interface, create_callback→closure, create_object→JS constructor, download_buffer→Blob+anchor click, force_fs_sync→IDBFS sync) and returning correct 'not available' results on native, so GDScript calls resolve on both targets.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript calling JavaScriptBridge.create_object/eval/get_interface resolves through the interpreter's singleton dispatch (not an 'unknown identifier' error), and download_buffer/force_fs_sync are callable with defined native fallbacks. (test: `javascript_bridge_singleton_script_reachable`) attaches a script that references JavaScriptBridge and asserts the calls dispatch and return the defined values rather than an interpreter unknown-singleton error.

title: OS.has_feature web tags + ProjectSettings .web override resolution
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web_feature_tags] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Real Godot projects branch heavily on OS.has_feature('web'|'wasm'|'JavaScript'|'threads'|'mobile'|'editor'|'debug') and ProjectSettings resolves per-feature overrides like `display/window/size/viewport_width.web`. Patina has no has_feature at all (grep empty; interpreter OS is 4 methods, interpreter.rs:6255) and never reports the web platform because the wasm branch (interpreter.rs:6268) is dead. Implementation: add OS.has_feature to the interpreter's OS singleton dispatch and to gdplatform/os.rs, returning the platform tags (web/wasm32/JavaScript on the wasm target; desktop tags on native), build config tags (debug/release, threads/simd from the web export config), plus editor when is_editor_hint; and honor `.web`-suffixed ProjectSettings overrides during project load. Note: general OS/has_feature breadth is shared with the platform-os subsystem; this bead covers the web/wasm/browser tags and the `.web` override path specifically.
acceptance_criteria: OS.has_feature('web') and OS.has_feature('wasm') return true under the wasm build and false on native, and a ProjectSettings value with a `.web` override resolves to the web-specific value when the web feature is active. title: Web networking: browser fetch/WebSocket/WebRTC bindings behind a transport abstraction + COOP/COEP
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web_networking] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

On the web target Godot routes HTTPClient/HTTPRequest through the browser fetch API (library_godot_fetch.js), WebSocketPeer through the browser WebSocket object, and WebRTCPeerConnection through RTCPeerConnection — because raw TCP/UDP sockets are unavailable in the browser. Patina's transports are all native sockets (http_client.rs std::net TcpStream; websocket_peer.rs native RFC6455, no wss; webrtc_peer.rs a stub) and are not exposed to GDScript. Implementation: introduce a transport abstraction so HTTPClient/HTTPRequest and WebSocketPeer select a browser-backed implementation under cfg(target_arch=wasm32) (fetch for HTTP, window.WebSocket for WS incl. wss, RTCPeerConnection/RTCDataChannel for WebRTC) while keeping the native impls for desktop; expose HTTPRequest/HTTPClient/WebSocketPeer as script-reachable classes; and have the editor server emit Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy/Embedder-Policy so a threaded web build can be previewed. Coordinate the WebSocket/WebRTC protocol surface with the multiplayer subsystem to avoid duplication.
acceptance_criteria: HTTPRequest and WebSocketPeer are constructible and callable from GDScript and dispatch to a transport chosen by target (browser fetch/WebSocket under wasm, native otherwise), and the editor server responds with COOP/COEP headers. (test: `web_http_websocket_script_reachable`) constructs HTTPRequest and WebSocketPeer from a script, asserts they resolve through the interpreter and select the correct transport, and asserts the editor server includes the cross-origin isolation headers.

title: Web I/O backends: fetch-based PCK loading, IndexedDB/OPFS user:// persistence, and AudioWorklet mixer sink
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web_assets_persistence] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot's web export fetches the .pck over HTTP with progress (preloader.js), persists user:// through emscripten IDBFS with an explicit sync (force_fs_sync), and drives audio through an AudioWorklet fed from the mixer (audio_driver_web.cpp, audio.worklet.js) unlocked on the first user gesture. Patina has none of these: no IndexedDB/OPFS/localStorage backend (grep empty; web.rs WebStorageBackend is a dead stub), no PCK-over-HTTP loader (only native pck.rs:674), and no AudioWorklet/AudioContext sink for gdaudio. Implementation (stage under cfg(target_arch=wasm32)): (1) a fetch-based ResourceLoader/PCK source that streams res:// assets over HTTP with progress into the existing loader; (2) a user:// FileAccess backend mapping to IndexedDB or OPFS with a force_fs_sync flush; (3) an AudioWorklet output that pulls the gdaudio mixer buffer (SharedArrayBuffer ring when cross-origin-isolated, message-port fallback otherwise) and resumes the AudioContext on first input. Keep the native filesystem/audio backends for desktop.
acceptance_criteria: On the web target a project boots by fetching its PCK over HTTP, user:// reads/writes round-trip through the browser storage backend across a simulated reload (with force_fs_sync flushing), and the audio mixer feeds an AudioWorklet sink resumed after a gesture. (test: `web_pck_fetch_and_user_persistence`) exercises the fetch-PCK loader and the IndexedDB/OPFS user:// backend behind the storage abstraction, asserting an asset loads and a user:// write survives a re-open.

title: ProjectSettings: honor physics tick rate + 2D/3D gravity from project.godot at boot
description:
[audit-key: project-settings-runtime-honoring-and-script-api/projectsettings-physics-honor] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

GODOT: At startup Godot reads physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second, physics/2d/default_gravity(+_vector) and physics/3d/default_gravity(+_vector) from project.godot and configures Engine.physics_ticks_per_second and the PhysicsServer2D/3D space gravity accordingly (upstream core/config/project_settings.cpp + physics servers). A project that sets 30 ticks or 490 gravity simulates at those values.

PATINA: The values are parsed but never honored. gdresource/src/project.rs:200-213 extracts them into ProjectConfig and ProjectLoader::load (project.rs:273) reads project.godot, but nothing in the runtime consumes ProjectConfig/ProjectLoader (grep of patina-runner/gdscene/gdscript-interop for from_project_file/ProjectLoader:: yields only defs+tests). patina-runner/src/main.rs:367 builds MainLoop::new(tree) which hardcodes 60 tps (main_loop.rs:178) and physics worlds default to (0,980)/(0,-9.8). set_physics_ticks_per_second/set_gravity are only ever called from #[cfg(test)] code.

APPROACH: In patina-runner (main.rs + bootstrap.rs BootConfig/init phases), locate project.godot via ProjectLoader::load(project_dir) (add a project_dir arg or derive from scene path), extract ProjectConfig, then: (1) pass physics_ticks_per_second into MainLoop (new ctor param or set_physics_ticks_per_second before running); (2) compute gravity = default_gravity * default_gravity_vector and forward into the internal PhysicsServer/PhysicsServer3D set_gravity via a new MainLoop::configure_from_project(&ProjectConfig). WIRING: boot(project) -> ProjectLoader -> MainLoop tick rate + physics world gravity, with NO manual setter in the test.
acceptance_criteria: Booting the runner on a project dir whose project.godot declares physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second=30 and physics/2d/default_gravity=490 yields main_loop.physics_ticks_per_second()==30, the 2D physics world gravity y==490, and a RigidBody2D falls at the project gravity (position after N frames matches 490 not 980) - all via the boot path, not a manual set_* call. (test: project_settings_physics_honored)

title: XR: WebXRInterface browser session lifecycle + stereo submit to XRWebGLLayer
description:
[audit-key: xr-peripheral/xr-webxr-binding] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: modules/webxr/webxr_interface_js.cpp implements an XRInterface over the browser navigator.xr API, registered with XRServer under the name "WebXR" (see WebXRInterface.xml codeblock). Because WebXR is callback-based, the interface is signal-driven: is_session_supported(mode) returns void and later emits session_supported(mode,supported); initialize() (from XRInterface) asynchronously requests a session and emits session_started or session_failed(message); session_ended fires on exit. Properties configure the request: session_mode ('immersive-vr'/'immersive-ar'/'inline'), required_features/optional_features, requested_reference_space_types -> resolved reference_space_type, enabled_features, visibility_state. Input sources map to selectstart/select/selectend + squeezestart/squeeze/squeezeend (each with input_source_id); get_input_source_tracker(id)->XRControllerTracker and get_input_source_target_ray_mode(id) (TargetRayMode GAZE/TRACKED_POINTER/SCREEN). display refresh rate get/set/available + display_refresh_rate_changed, reference_space_reset, visibility_state_changed. Rendering: on session_started the app sets get_viewport().use_xr=true; the browser XRSession.requestAnimationFrame drives the frame loop and each eye's XRView pose+projection is submitted into the session XRWebGLLayer framebuffer.

Patina current state: none. Grep for webxr/immersive/requestSession/navigator.xr across crates and apps is empty; WebXRInterface unregistered.

Implementation approach: depends on the XRServer scaffolding (group xr-core-scene). Add a WebXRInterface implementation with wasm-bindgen bindings to navigator.xr in the gdplatform web layer (gdplatform/src/xr.rs + a web-cfg module), registered with XRServer as "WebXR"; back the async signals with browser Promise/event callbacks; translate XRInputSource select/squeeze events into the signals and feed XRController3D via XRControllerTracker poses read from the XRFrame. When Viewport.use_xr is set, drive patina-runner's frame loop from XRSession.requestAnimationFrame and render two eyes (per-XRView projection+view) into the XRWebGLLayer through gdrender3d. On native/non-web, is_session_supported must report unsupported (correct no-op) rather than panic.

Wiring requirement (end-to-end): patina-runner boot -> script gets XRServer.find_interface("WebXR") -> is_session_supported emits session_supported -> initialize() calls navigator.xr.requestSession -> session_started -> get_viewport().use_xr=true switches the runner render loop to the XR rAF submitting stereo frames; input sources fire select/squeeze and XRController3D signals every XR frame.
acceptance_criteria: With a stubbed navigator.xr, a script obtaining XRServer.find_interface("WebXR") and calling is_session_supported("immersive-vr") receives a session_supported(mode,supported) signal; setting session_mode/required_features and calling initialize() emits session_started and flips get_viewport().use_xr to true, and a mock input-source select event emits the `select` signal with its input_source_id whose get_input_source_tracker returns an XRControllerTracker. Test proves the interface is registered, added to XRServer, and its signal/property round-trip happens from a script (not module internals) (test: `webxr_interface_session_lifecycle_signals`). Live-browser stereo submit is verified by the build/browser verifier lane.

description:

comments.author: RedTower
comments.text: Triage (RedTower, no-run analysis): the IK math + skeleton API already exist — gdscene/src/ik_solver.rs has solve_fabrik(joints,target,iters,tol)->Vec<Vector3>, solve_two_bone_ik, and aim_rotation(from,to)->Quaternion; gdscene/src/skeleton3d.rs has the full bone API (get_bone_count/get_bone_global_pose/set_bone_pose/get_bone_parent/get_bone_children/set_bone_pose_rotation). Remaining work is additive: (1) register SkeletonModifier3D(<-Node3D) + IKModifier3D(<-SkeletonModifier3D) in class_db.rs; (2) an IKModifier3D model (target Vector3, chain root/tip bone idxs, influence f32); (3) run it in the skeleton-update phase: read chain joints' global-pose origins, solve_fabrik, then write each solved global position back as a LOCAL bone pose via parent_global.affine_inverse()*new_global (rotation from aim_rotation toward the next joint), processed root->tip; (4) test asserting tip global pose distance-to-target decreases, blended by influence. NOT taken by a no-cargo worker: the global->local frame write-back is geometry-correctness-sensitive and can't be verified without running (a wrong Transform3D method would break the shared gdscene crate). A cargo-capable worker should take it.

comments.author: GentleBadger
comments.text: DELIVERED by GentleBadger (2026-07-16, uncommitted; verify cmds in completion mail msg 55108). ACCEPTANCE MET: SkeletonModifier3D (abstract, parent Node3D) + IKModifier3D (parent SkeletonModifier3D) ClassDB-registered next to Skeleton3D; an IKModifier3D under a Skeleton3D drives the chain tip toward its target, blended by influence, without detaching intermediate bones. The named acceptance test ik_modifier3d_drives_bone_chain_tip_toward_target NOW EXISTS (gdscene/tests/, 5 tests). This bead was flagged [unverified] (triage sweep) and its claim CHECKS OUT — skeleton3d.rs genuinely had no modifier machinery. WHY AN INTEGRATION TEST rather than '-p gdscene --lib': '--test <name>' compiles the LIBRARY WITHOUT cfg(test), so it sidesteps gdscene's unit-test target (red from foreign WIP) entirely; it is also a target selector, so it hard-errors if missing and a PASS proves it really ran. DESIGN: process_modifiers(tree, skeleton_id) runs the stack (Godot: modifiers process AFTER AnimationPlayer/Tree writes poses, so IK layers on top instead of being overwritten), skipping inactive ones; CCD solver over the chain; bone_chain() returns EMPTY when the tip does not descend from the root, so a mis-wired modifier is a no-op rather than mangling unrelated bones. 'No detaching' holds BY CONSTRUCTION: the solver only writes bone ROTATIONS and a bone's global pose is composed from its parents, so parent->child offsets are preserved automatically (test pins each bone at exactly 1.0 from its parent after 16 iterations, which also proves no scale drift through repeated basis multiplication). THE SUBTLE BIT — poses live in the bone's PARENT frame, so a skeleton-space rotation delta becomes: pose' = (parent_basis*rest_basis)^-1 * delta * (parent_basis*rest_basis) * pose. Influence scales each CCD correction angle: 0 = untouched (early return), 1 = full solve, between = partway. *** GEOMETRY GOTCHA (a reviewer caught this by NUMERICALLY SIMULATING the solver — it would have FAILED the verify): bone0 is the FIXED PIVOT at (0,1,0) because a joint's own pose rotation swings its DESCENDANTS, never itself. So a 3-bone chain with 1-unit rests has reach 2, NOT 3. My original target (3,0,0) sits ~3.16 from the pivot = unreachable; the tip converges to ~1.16 away and assert!(after < 0.1) fails. Retargeted the acceptance test to (1,1,0). *** The influence test DELIBERATELY keeps the unreachable (3,0,0): against a reachable target both influence 0.5 and 1.0 converge to ~0 and the strict full<half ordering TIES and fails — keeping it out of reach is what makes the blend observable. Documented in-place. NOT COMPILED by me (worker build policy). REMAINING (follow-ons, not acceptance blockers): (1) process_modifiers is caller-driven — it still needs invoking from the frame loop after the pose update for IK to run in a live scene; (2) the modification_processed signal is registered but never emitted (nothing emits engine->script signals yet — see pat-nzgdu.150); (3) Godot's richer surface: target NODE/BONE (I model target_position only), bone constraints/limits, FABRIK as an alternative solver (the bead allows CCD or FABRIK; I chose CCD); (4) sibling beads pat-nzgdu.182/.183 build on this base. ALSO RE-FLAGGING a pre-existing red test I do not own: tests/misc_suite_d/node3d_runtime_slice_test.rs:125 asserts class_count()==12 after register_3d_classes, which already makes 125 registrations — red long before this bead (reported on pat-nzgdu.140); my 2 new classes do not newly break a passing test.

description:
[audit-key: audio/audio/stream-playback-runtime-family] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

Model Godot's playback-instance layer: AudioStreamPlayback (<-RefCounted) as the runtime object returned by AudioStream.instantiate_playback(), AudioStreamPlaybackResampled with the sample-rate conversion base, and the per-stream subclasses (OggVorbis, GeneratorPlayback with push_buffer, Interactive, Playlist, Polyphonic, Synchronized). Register all in ClassDB. The existing stream.rs AudioStreamPlayback state-machine can back the base, but must gain frame-producing mix() semantics tied to a source AudioStream.

(test: `audiostream_playback_instances_registered_and_produce_frames`)

comments.author: GentleBadger
comments.text: PARTIAL by GentleBadger (2026-07-16, uncommitted; verify cmds in completion mail msg 55210). DELIVERED 3 of the acceptance's 4 clauses. The bead was [unverified] (triage sweep) and its 'PARTIAL' status is ACCURATE — AudioStreamGenerator + PolyphonicPlayer did already exist in gdaudio/src/decode.rs, and stream.rs's AudioStreamPlayback state machine is real; none of the family was in ClassDB. CLAUSE 1 (ClassDB family) DONE: 8 classes with Godot's real shape — AudioStreamPlayback is an abstract RefCounted, NOT a Resource (Godot separates the stream RESOURCE from the playback INSTANCE it hands out); AudioStreamPlaybackResampled sits abstract between the base and the DECODER playbacks (OggVorbis, Generator) that need rate conversion, while the CONTAINER playbacks (Polyphonic/Interactive/Playlist/Synchronized) derive the base DIRECTLY because they mix children that are already resampled. The test asserts that distinction BOTH ways (containers must NOT derive Resampled). Needed a RefCounted bootstrap guard in register_audio_classes, which only had Object/Node. CLAUSE 2 (push_buffer + mix) DONE: push_buffer is ALL-OR-NOTHING (Godot rejects an oversized push rather than partially filling — a torn push tears the signal) plus frames_available/can_push_buffer/clear_buffer. THE IMPORTANT PART: the new mix() CONSUMES. The pre-existing mix_to_buffer only PEEKS at the whole queue and leaves it in place, so a generator wired to it would replay stale audio forever instead of refilling; mix(n) drains, under-runs to silence rather than erroring. CLAUSE 3 (polyphonic) DONE: PolyphonicPlayer previously only COUNTED voices — try_play() incremented an integer and no audio was ever summed. It now holds real sub-playbacks and mix(n) sums them frame-for-frame; finished voices contribute silence for the rest of the block then are RETIRED, freeing their slot, so a finished one-shot cannot pin the pool at its limit forever. Output is deliberately NOT clamped — mixing is additive, headroom is the bus's job (Godot's mix stage). BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: new() arities unchanged; push_frame/mix_to_buffer/try_play untouched; existing generator_and_poly test still passes; nothing outside decode.rs constructs either struct with a literal, so the new private field is safe. 7 new tests. NOT COMPILED by me (worker build policy) — eye-verified + reviewer pass. KEEP OPEN — REMAINING: (1) CLAUSE 4 instantiate_playback() is BLOCKED: there is NO AudioStream resource type in the tree at all (grep empty) — only AudioBuffer + decoders. It needs the resource layer first (AudioStream + AudioStreamWAV/AudioStreamOggVorbis with instantiate_playback() returning a playback bound to the decoded buffer). That is a design step, not a slice. (2) AudioStreamPlaybackResampled does no resampling yet — registered only; server.rs's mixer resamples (mix_resamples_low_rate_stream_to_output_rate), the playback-level base does not. (3) stream.rs's AudioStreamPlayback state machine (play/pause/seek/advance) is still NOT tied to frame production — needs (1) first. (4) Interactive/Playlist/Synchronized are CLASS SURFACE ONLY — no clip switching, playlist ordering or sync logic. (5) The acceptance test audiostream_playback_instances_registered_and_produce_frames DOES NOT EXIST — do not trust a stale-recovery close (0-match filters exit 0).

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED (mail 55494). All 4 acceptance clauses met.

BLOCKER ON THE STATED APPROACH (the description is not implementable):
The bead says 'backed by / over the existing UndoRedoManager'. UndoRedoManager lives in
gdeditor/src/undo_redo.rs, and gdeditor/Cargo.toml:27 depends on gdscript-interop. So gdeditor
depends on gdscript-interop; binding the interpreter to gdeditor's UndoRedoManager would invert
that into a dependency CYCLE, which the build system hard-errors on. It cannot be done as written.

ROUTE TAKEN: interpreter-local handle mirroring the existing CameraFeed pattern (pat-nzgdu.179) —
the established precedent for Object-style script handles that are not nodes. Handle tag 0xED
(non-colliding with 0xCF ConfigFile / 0xFA FileAccess / 0xDA DirAccess / 0xCA CameraFeed).
Property writes apply through SceneAccess::set_node_property (bindings.rs:207), so commit/undo/redo
genuinely mutate the scene rather than only recording history.

CONSEQUENCE worth its own bead: there are now TWO undo/redo impls — gdeditor's UndoRedoManager
(editor-internal) and this script-visible one. Unifying needs a shared undo/redo crate BELOW both.
I did not expand scope to do it.

Files:
- engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs (UndoRedo registration in register_io_classes)
- engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs (handle + new() dispatch + instance dispatch)
- engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/tests/undoredo_class_commit_undo_redo_property.rs (NEW, 5 tests)

Verify: -p gdscript-interop --test undoredo_class_commit_undo_redo_property
        -p gdobject --lib class_db

MERGE_ENDS semantics (matches Godot undo_redo.cpp): the previous action's do-ops are REPLACED by
the new ones and the ORIGINAL undo-ops are KEPT — so undoing a merged pair returns to the state
before the FIRST action. Test asserts Move(0->10)+Move(10->20) coalesces to one entry and undo
lands on 0, not 10. The test observes the SCENE via a recording SceneAccess mock, not the history,
so it fails if ops are recorded but never applied.

DELIBERATELY NOT REGISTERED: add_do_method / add_undo_method / add_do_reference. They must invoke a
Callable, which needs re-entry into the interpreter; the op recorder is a free fn with no
&mut Interpreter. Registering them would make class_has_method() promise a method that errors on
call. Registered surface == implemented surface: 15 and 15, verified mechanically.

REMAINING (do not let a close imply these are done):
- method-ops / reference-ops (needs an interpreter-re-entrant op recorder)
- version_changed signal registered but never emitted (no engine->script signal path)
- commit_action(execute=false) honored but untested
- UndoRedo.MERGE_ENDS as a direct static-member access does NOT resolve; only the
  ClassDB.class_get_integer_constant reflection path works (which the test uses)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — COMPILE FIX (E0521) applied to my UndoRedo code; resend-worthy, please re-verify.

A verifier run on a DIFFERENT bead (pat-u3l8c.12) exposed a real compile error in MY .155 code:
  error: could not compile gdscript-interop (lib) due to 1 previous error -- E0521
The verifier builds the WORKING TREE (it compiled an untracked test file), so my uncommitted
interpreter.rs changes were in that build and broke every downstream crate's test compile.

THE BUG: my helper took  fn apply(ops: &[PropOp], access: &mut Option<&mut dyn SceneAccess>).
The field is  scene_access: Option<Box<dyn SceneAccess>>  (interpreter.rs:388). A Box<dyn Trait>
with NO enclosing reference carries an implicit '+ 'static'. Wrapping the Option in a SECOND &mut
makes its pointee INVARIANT, forcing the trait object's lifetime to unify with BOTH the reborrow of
self AND 'static -> 'self escapes' = E0521.

THE FIX: take the Option BY VALUE -> fn apply(ops: &[PropOp], access: Option<&mut dyn SceneAccess>).
The three call sites (commit_action/undo/redo) are mutually exclusive match arms, so access moves at
most once per path. The single-layer shape is proven sound by accumulate_vec2_property
(interpreter.rs:6080-6168), which already feeds the same field into &mut dyn SceneAccess and compiles
today.

RULE WORTH KEEPING: never nest &mut around an Option/struct holding a &mut dyn Trait. One layer is
fine and is the established pattern here; two layers collide with the Box's implicit 'static.

Verify (unchanged): -p gdscript-interop --test undoredo_class_commit_undo_redo_property
                    -p gdobject --lib class_db

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — CORRECTION to my previous comment; resent (mail 55918).

MY EARLIER COMMENT'S MECHANISM WAS WRONG. It blamed a nested &mut Option<&mut dyn SceneAccess> and
'fixed' it by taking the Option by value. The verifier proved that wrong — the SAME E0521 came back
and the bead pat-u3l8c.12 got PARKED as collateral. Do not follow that earlier advice.

THE ACTUAL CAUSE: an Option-wrapped trait object with an ELIDED lifetime.
  field:  scene_access: Option<Box<dyn SceneAccess>>   // Box<dyn _> with no enclosing reference
                                                       // => implicit '+ 'static'
  so:     self.scene_access.as_deref_mut()  ->  Option<&'r mut (dyn SceneAccess + 'static)>
                                                 ('r = a reborrow of self)
  param:  Option<&mut dyn SceneAccess>      ==  Option<&'x mut (dyn SceneAccess + 'x)>
Coercions do NOT reach inside a generic constructor like Option, so the types must match by
SUBTYPING. &mut is INVARIANT in its pointee => (dyn SceneAccess + 'static) must EQUAL
(dyn SceneAccess + 'x) => 'x = 'static => 'r = 'static => self escapes => E0521.

THE FIX: name the bound, which the boxed accessor genuinely has:
  access: Option<&mut (dyn SceneAccess + 'static)>
Pointees are then equal, leaving only the covariant 'r: 'x.

WHY THIS ONE IS TRUSTWORTHY (precedent, not reasoning):
  gdplatform/src/network.rs:289 — committed, clean, compiling:
    pub fn peer_mut(&mut self) -> Option<&mut (dyn NetworkPeer + 'static)> { self.peer.as_deref_mut() }
  Same field shape (Option<Box<dyn _>>), same as_deref_mut, 'static spelled out.
  And there are ZERO elided 'Option<&mut dyn Trait>' params anywhere in the workspace — exactly what
  you'd expect if the shape cannot compile.
A bare '&mut dyn SceneAccess' param IS fine (accumulate_vec2_property, interpreter.rs:38/53) because
its callers pass '&mut **access' — a fresh reborrow, which IS a coercion site. The Option wrapper is
what removes that opportunity.

TECHNIQUE WORTH KEEPING: grep for the signature shape BEFORE trusting a derivation. Two separate
code-reviewer passes got this wrong (one blessed the original; one blessed the bad fix). When you
cannot compile, only an in-repo compiling precedent counts.

Verify (unchanged): -p gdscript-interop --test undoredo_class_commit_undo_redo_property
                    -p gdobject --lib class_db

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED PARTIAL (mail 56183): 2 of 3 acceptance clauses. Do NOT let a close imply clause 3.

CLAUSE 1 DONE: ClassDB::class_exists('RichTextEffect'). Registered RichTextEffect (parent Resource)
+ CharFXTransform (parent RefCounted) in register_2d_classes. RefCounted was NOT registered anywhere
in that fn — an unregistered base silently severs the chain from Object (the pat-nzgdu.98 trap), so
I bootstrap it and the test asserts both classes reach Object, not just their immediate parent.

CLAUSE 2 DONE: [wave]...[/wave] offsets glyph positions per frame. New gdscene::char_fx module:
CharFXTransform + all six built-ins (wave/tornado/shake/fade/rainbow/pulse) as PURE functions of

with per-glyph offset/colour; untagged text keeps the single-draw fast path.

independent reasons:
  1. the render pass holds &SceneTree; calling a script needs &mut
  2. RichTextLabel has no custom_effects property, and nothing maps a bbcode tag -> an effect's bbcode
  3. CharFXTransform has no Variant encoding, so it cannot cross
     ScriptInstance::call_method(&[Variant]) and come back mutated
  4. ResourceRef { path, class_name, properties } has NO script slot; the only script-attachment path
     (instantiate_script) models a scripted 'Resource' as a phantom Node under the scene root
Any ONE blocks it. I did NOT fake a seam: [ghost] degrades to plain text (asserted) rather than
inventing a non-Godot node-based effect model that would have to be torn out later.

TEST-NAMING HONESTY: the named test richtext_effect_custom_fx_test exists and passes but covers the
REGISTRATION + BUILT-IN halves. unknown_and_custom_effect_tags_are_stripped_not_rendered asserts
today's real behaviour (ghost -> one plain run). When clause 3 lands that test must be REPLACED, not
extended — true acceptance is 3 per-glyph draws with the script invoked.

REVIEWER CAUGHT A REAL BUG PRE-SHIP: a nested tag splits an effected run into several spans
([wave]a[color=red]b[/color]c[/wave] = 3), and I computed each sub-run's range from its OWN bounds ->
relative_index restarted at 0 per piece -> glyphs bobbed in phase instead of travelling. Fixed by
backfilling each effect application's true range across all its runs; added the missing regression
test (effect_phase_continues_across_a_nested_tag). Verified numerically: split and unsplit now give
identical offsets [0, 2.397, 4.207, 4.987].

DELIBERATE DEVIATION (documented in-code): Godot phases wave/tornado by the glyph's PIXEL X
(sin(elapsed*freq + glyph_x/50)), coupling the effect to font metrics + wrapping. I phase by
relative_index — same visual, reproducible from the char index, which is what makes it assertable.
Tag names/params/defaults match Godot. [shake] hashes (time step, index) instead of an RNG so it is
stable within a step and testable.

Verify: -p gdscene --test richtext_effect_custom_fx_test
        -p gdscene --lib char_fx
        -p gdscene --lib control_render
        -p gdobject --lib class_db

title: Rendering2D: wire SceneTree -> canvas pipeline with global transforms and z/y-sort draw order
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/canvas-pipeline-core] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot draws every CanvasItem-derived node each frame through RenderingServer canvas commands, honoring the node's GLOBAL Transform2D (position*rotation*scale composed up the parent chain), z_index+z_as_relative global ordering, y_sort_enabled cross-parent ordering, and modulate/self_modulate propagation (scene/main/canvas_item.cpp). Patina has none of this in any runtime: the canvas pipeline (gdserver2d::canvas + gdrender2d::renderer::SoftwareRenderer) has zero scene-node producers (grep 'DrawCommand::' hits only tests), patina-runner is headless (main.rs:273-397, no gdrender2d dep), and the only wired 2D surface — the editor viewport via examples/editor.rs:372 -> scene_renderer.rs:213-277 — draws icons at LOCAL position (extract_position, scene_renderer.rs:220) with no rotation/scale/parent composition and no z-order draw sort, despite gdscene::node2d::get_global_transform (node2d.rs:83) already existing. Implement a scene->canvas render bridge (new module, e.g. gdrender2d::scene_bridge with a gdscene dep, or promote the editor's renderer): walk tree in order, compute each node's global Transform2D via node2d::get_global_transform, build CanvasItems ordered by accumulated z_index (respect z_as_relative) then y_sort within a subtree then tree order, propagate modulate*self_modulate and visible/visible_in_tree, feed gdserver2d::Viewport + SoftwareRenderer::render_frame to a FrameData, and replace the schematic path in examples/editor.rs so the live editor viewport shows the real transformed/ordered scene. Expose the same entry as the public 2D render for the web runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn whose root Node2D is rotated 45deg and translated, containing a Sprite2D child plus two overlapping ColorRects with z_index 0 and 1, renders (a) the sprite pixels at the globally-rotated+translated location (not the local position) and (b) the z_index=1 rect fully on top of the z_index=0 rect. The editor /api/viewport frame reflects parent rotation. Prove wiring end-to-end from PackedScene::from_tscn to FrameData pixels. (test: `scene_canvas_render_bridge`)

All 10 classes registered in register_viewport_classes -> register_rendering_device_classes():
RenderingDevice(Object), RDShaderSource(RefCounted), RDShaderSPIRV(Resource), RDShaderFile(Resource),
RDUniform, RDTextureFormat, RDTextureView, RDSamplerState, RDVertexAttribute,

so I bootstrap it and the test asserts every RD* class REACHES Object, not just its parent.

  1. NO GLSL->SPIRV compiler anywhere in the workspace (no shaderc/naga/spirv-* in any Cargo.toml).

title: Add MissingNode/MissingResource to preserve unknown classes losslessly on scene round-trip
description:

[audit-key: sweep-7/resources-io/missing-placeholders] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** When a .tscn/.tres references a class/script the engine doesn't recognize, Godot instantiates a MissingNode/MissingResource that stores the original_class name + all raw properties, so re-saving the file preserves the data byte-for-byte instead of dropping it. doc/classes/MissingNode.xml, MissingResource.xml.

**Patina today:** neither class exists (grep matches are unrelated test names in compare3d.rs/export.rs/property_undo.rs). An unknown class today has no preservation path, risking silent data loss on load→save — exactly the failure the resources-io stones forbid ("NO silent skips of unparseable values").

**Implement:** Add MissingNode (Node) and MissingResource (Resource) holding original_class + a property bag; make the .tscn/.tres loader (gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs, gdresource/src/loader.rs) emit them for unrecognized types and the saver re-emit the stored class + properties verbatim.

**Wiring requirement:** Load a .tscn referencing an unknown class into a MissingNode and save it back with the original type string + properties intact.

**Prove it:** Round-trip a .tscn containing an unregistered node type; assert the re-saved text preserves the original class name and every property (no drops).
acceptance_criteria: Loading a scene/resource that references an unknown class produces a MissingNode/MissingResource retaining original_class + all properties, and re-saving reproduces the original type and properties losslessly (test: `unknown_class_preserved_via_missing_node_roundtrip`).

title: Resources/Boot: boot patina-runner from project.godot (main scene, autoloads, input map, ProjectSettings, res:// root)
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/project-boot] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot boots a project by parsing project.godot: it resolves application/run/main_scene, registers [autoload] scene/script singletons, installs the [input] InputMap actions, applies config/features (incl. .web overrides), and populates the ProjectSettings singleton the runtime honors (physics/rendering/audio). Patina's runner (patina-runner/src/main.rs) instead takes a raw .tscn path and ignores project.godot entirely; the parsers that exist (gdresource/src/project.rs ProjectLoader, gdcore/src/project_settings.rs ProjectSettings::load_godot_project) are library-only with no runtime caller, and gdcore::file_access::set_path_roots is never invoked so res:///user:// cannot resolve. Implement a boot path that: (1) if given a project dir/project.godot, calls ProjectLoader::load + ProjectSettings::load_godot_project, (2) calls gdcore::set_path_roots(project_root, user_root) so FileAccess res:// works, (3) resolves main_scene and loads it via the scene loader, (4) instantiates autoloads before the main scene, (5) installs the input map into gdplatform input. Wire this into patina-runner/src/main.rs and patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs init_resources()/init_main_scene().
acceptance_criteria: Running the runner against a fixtures project dir containing project.godot (with run/main_scene, an [autoload], and an [input] action) boots the declared main scene, the autoload node exists in the tree, res:// FileAccess resolves under the project root, and ProjectSettings.get_setting reflects a project.godot value. (test: `runner_boots_project_godot`)

title: Physics3D: implement PhysicalBone3D + PhysicalBoneSimulator3D ragdoll driven by MainLoop
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/physics3d-ragdoll] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ragdolls use PhysicalBoneSimulator3D (a SkeletonModifier3D) plus PhysicalBone3D bodies joint-connected per skeleton bone; physical_bones_start_simulation() hands skeleton pose control to the physics bodies, which are stepped and write their transforms back to the Skeleton3D bone poses. Patina has neither class (unregistered.txt; no struct in gdphysics3d). Implementation: register PhysicalBone3D (parent PhysicsBody3D) and PhysicalBoneSimulator3D (SkeletonModifier3D); create rigid bodies per PhysicalBone3D connected by joints (depends on the joints bead), and on start_simulation drive the parent Skeleton3D bone global poses from the simulated body transforms each physics frame; on stop, return control to the animation pose. Wiring: stepped by MainLoop's physics sub-step and applied to Skeleton3D poses the renderer consumes.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn Skeleton3D with PhysicalBone3D bodies under a PhysicalBoneSimulator3D, with simulation started, run through MainLoop::step under gravity, moves the skeleton bone global poses (a bone's global position falls) instead of staying at the rest pose. title: EngineDebugger: expose script singleton and wire runner→editor remote debug/profiler over WebSocket
description:
[audit-key: platform-os/engine-debugger] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot ground truth: EngineDebugger is script-callable (is_active, register_profiler, profiler_add_frame_data, register_message_capture, send_message, insert_breakpoint) and, more importantly, the running game speaks a remote-debug protocol to the editor so breakpoints/stack/locals, error trees, and profiler frames appear live in the editor debugger panel (upstream core/debugger/, editor/debugger/). Patina current state: EngineDebugger is not script-reachable (0 interpreter dispatch); gdcore/src/debugger.rs and debug_protocol.rs implement the pieces but are only referenced by gdcore/src/lib.rs — nothing connects a running game to the editor, and gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs (419-443) holds its own disconnected debug/profiler state. Approach: add an EngineDebugger singleton dispatch arm in interpreter.rs over gdcore debugger; establish the debug_protocol channel (WebSocket in the browser-native model) between the runner and the editor server so breakpoints hit in the runner surface in the editor and profiler frames stream into editor_server profiler_frames. Wiring requirement: a breakpoint set in the editor pauses the running scene and its stack is reported back over the protocol. (Note: this overlaps editor-ux for the panel UI; this bead owns the EngineDebugger singleton + protocol transport.)
acceptance_criteria: A headless test starts the debug protocol between a runner instance and a mock editor endpoint, sets a breakpoint on a script line, runs a .tscn whose script reaches that line, and asserts the editor side receives a break message with the correct script/line and a stack frame — plus `EngineDebugger.is_active()` returns true from a script under the debug session. (test: `engine_debugger_remote_protocol_e2e`)

comments.text:

Does NOT meet acceptance: no break message crosses the protocol, no .tscn run.

EngineDebugger appeared NOWHERE in the workspace (zero hits). gdcore/src/debugger.rs (536 lines) +
debug_protocol.rs (869 lines) COMPILE but were referenced only by gdcores own lib.rs. Two healthy

implemented — they need the break machinery; they fall to UndefinedFunction.)

*** ARG-ORDER TRAP (tested BOTH ways) ***
Godot: insert_breakpoint(line: int, source: StringName) — LINE FIRST.
gdcore: BreakpointLocation::new(script, line) — SCRIPT FIRST.
Both args come out of &[Variant], so swapping them is NOT a compile error — it silently registers a

AND that no script named "12" exists.

title: Editor/Resources: lossless .tscn save — regenerate ext_resource/sub_resource tables, uid+load_steps header, and full Variant serialization
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/tscn-save] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot's text saver round-trips a scene exactly: it collects external resource references (scripts, textures, sub-scenes) into an [ext_resource] table with ids, inline sub-resources into [sub_resource] sections, writes a header with load_steps and uid=, and serializes every Variant type in canonical .tscn syntax. Patina's TscnSaver (gdscene/scene_saver.rs:134) drops ext/sub-resource sections entirely and Debug-formats unsupported Variants, so any real scene (one with a script, texture, material, shape, or instanced child) is corrupted on save. Fix: reconstruct the ext_resource/sub_resource tables from node references and __resref__ companions during save, emit the load_steps/uid header, write script/instance as unquoted ExtResource("id"), and extend format_variant_value to cover Vector2i/Vector3i/Vector4(i)/Transform3D/Basis/Quaternion/Plane/AABB/Projection/Packed* arrays.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a complex .tscn (root with a script ext_resource, a child instancing a sub-scene, a node with an inline sub_resource and a Transform3D property), saving it via TscnSaver, and re-parsing yields the same ext_resources, sub_resources, script path, instance ref, and Transform3D value as the original (round-trip diff is empty for those). (test: `tscn_save_roundtrip_ext_and_sub_resources`)

THE BEADS PREMISE IS STALE IN TWO LOAD-BEARING WAYS:

        -p gdscene --test fabrik3d_chain_reaches_target

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED (mail 58698): class surface + the grids ACCUMULATION. KEEP OPEN.
Editor-viewport DRAWING and .tscn/animation_path resolution are follow-up.

*** BIG FIND FOR EVERY WORKER: GODOTS FULL C++ SOURCE IS VENDORED IN-TREE AT upstream/godot/ ***
2189 .cpp files. extension_api.json gives SCHEMA, doc_classes XML gives DEFAULTS — NEITHER can tell you
what the code DOES. This can, exactly. For ANY bead whose acceptance is BEHAVIOURAL ("drives",
"scrolls", "converges", "restores"), read the upstream .cpp rather than inferring from property names.
Cite file:line so the next agent can check you.

BUG IT CAUGHT IN MY OWN CODE: I wrapped the grid offset on ALL THREE AXES by reasoning. Godots
RootMotionView::_notification (root_motion_view.cpp:124-128) wraps X and Z ONLY and NEVER Y — Y is the
height of a flat grid, there are no cells along it. My doc comment claimed "mirrors Godot" — BACKWARDS.
The test that should have caught it was itself broken: y=0.5 against a 1.0 cell, where rem_euclid is
the IDENTITY — blind to the very bug it existed for. Now y=1.5, load-bearing.

*** THE BEADS DESCRIPTION INVENTS use_custom_color ***
Godot 4.6.1 has NO such property. RootMotionView declares EXACTLY five: animation_path, cell_size,
color, radius, zero_y. A test asserts the surface is EXACTLY those five — that is what refuses it.
Registering it would mean a .tscn that will not round-trip in Godot.

animation_path empty, color=Color(0.5,0.5,1,1) — a PALE BLUE, not white: the grid must read as a gizmo
rather than as geometry. Getter is get_zero_y NOT is_zero_y — Godot breaks its own bool-getter idiom
here (confirmed root_motion_view.cpp:187).
Wrapping with rem_euclid is VERIFIED PARITY: Math::fposmod (math_funcs.h:287) is byte-for-byte
rem_euclid for a positive divisor.

The grid test drives the REAL AnimationPlayer::consume_root_motion — the same call the runtime makes —
not hand-made deltas. A grid scrolling on invented numbers would look identical and prove nothing. It
also pins the inverse: an animation with NO root-motion track leaves the grid STILL.

REVIEWER CAUGHT 2 MORE THAT WOULD HAVE FAILED THE RUN:
1. My headline test would have PANICKED: with cell_size=4, accumulated z of exactly 4.0 wraps to 0.0,
   landing precisely ON the cell boundary. Deterministic (exact binary floats), not tolerance. Now 8.
2. E0451 — the file would NOT COMPILE: RootMotionView{cell_size: 4.0, ..RootMotionView::new()} needs
   EVERY field visible and `accumulated` is private, so struct-update syntax is illegal from another
   crate. The in-file unit tests use the identical pattern LEGALLY (mod tests is a descendant of the
   defining module) — which is exactly why it slipped past me. Now a plain field assignment.

Verify: -p gdobject --test root_motion_view_registration
        -p gdscene --test root_motion_view_grid_test
        -p gdscene --lib root_motion_view
        -p gdobject --lib class_db

4. DELIBERATE DEVIATION (stated as such, never "mirrors"): Godot keeps NO unwrapped travel — it wraps

title: Add SubtweenTweener (Tween.tween_subtween) nested-tween stepping
description:
[audit-key: animation/animation/subtween-tweener] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

[audit-key: sweep-13/animation/subtween-tweener] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** Tween.tween_subtween(subtween) appends a SubtweenTweener (<-Tweener) that runs an entire nested Tween as one step of the parent sequence, blocking the parent's chain until the sub-tween finishes (respecting parallel/chain semantics).

**Patina today:** Tween is wired into the frame loop (crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:425 -> process_tweens at scene_tree.rs:1307) but the builder only supports property tweens (crates/gdscene/src/tween.rs:442 tween_property); there is no tween_subtween and no Tweener hierarchy, so a nested tween cannot be sequenced.

**Implement:** Extend the TweenStep model in tween.rs with a Subtween step holding a nested Tween, and have Tween::advance drive the nested tween to completion before advancing the parent chain; expose tween_subtween on the builder and wire it through the existing process_tweens advance.

**Wiring requirement:** From a script in a runner scene, `create_tween().tween_subtween(inner)` must run `inner` to completion at the correct point in the parent sequence, with the parent chain waiting on it.

**Prove it:** App-level test builds a parent tween that tween_subtweens an inner property tween, advances process_tweens across the combined duration, and asserts the inner property animates and the parent step after it only starts once the sub-tween finished.
acceptance_criteria: A Tween using tween_subtween runs the nested Tween to completion before its next chained step begins, and the nested property animates to its end value when process_tweens is advanced across the total duration (test: `subtween_tweener_nested_test`)

comments.text:

*** THE HEADLINE: AudioSample + AudioSamplePlayback register with NOTHING but a parent, and that is
EXACT, not laziness. ***
Both are plain data structs with GDCLASS(..., RefCounted) and NO _bind_methods()
(upstream/godot/servers/audio/audio_stream.h:43-74). They ARE GDREGISTER_CLASS-d
(servers/register_server_types.cpp:171-172), so ClassDB knows name+parent — but every field is a public
C++ MEMBER, not a bound property. Their doc XMLs have NO <members>, <methods> or <constants> at all.

ClassDB/GDScript. Registering stream/loop_mode/pitch_scale would have INVENTED SCHEMA.
