title: Resources: implement real load()/preload()/ResourceLoader.load (text .tscn/.tres/images) wired through the GDScript interpreter
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/resource-load] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]
[verify-note: ADJUSTED: STUB is overstated and one factual claim is false. TRUE: the preload/load builtin (interpreter.rs:2389-2426) returns a path-only ResourceRef with an extension-guessed class_name and properties:HashMap::new(), so load('.tres').get(prop) and image pixels are genuinely NOT loaded. FALSE: 'the]

In Godot, load("res://x.tres") reads+parses the file and returns a live Resource; load("res://x.tscn") returns a PackedScene whose instantiate() builds the real subtree; load("res://x.png") returns a Texture2D backed by decoded pixels. Patina's interpreter (interpreter.rs:2389) returns a path-only placeholder with a guessed class string and never touches the filesystem. Implement a ResourceLoader backend that resolves res:// via gdcore::resolve_path, dispatches by extension to the existing loaders (gdresource TresLoader for .tres, gdscene PackedScene::from_tscn for .tscn, gdresource::import_image/texture_import for images), caches by path (gdresource::cache::ResourceCache), and returns Variants carrying the loaded resource. Expose ResourceLoader.load/exists/get_dependencies as a script singleton and route preload/load builtins through it so preload("x.tscn").instantiate() yields the real nodes and load("x.tres").get("prop") returns parsed properties.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript that runs load("res://sub.tres") reads a real property value from the parsed .tres, and preload("res://child.tscn").instantiate() adds the child scene's actual node subtree to the tree (verified via the runner tree dump). (test: `gdscript_load_reads_real_resource`)

title: Resources: complete the .tscn/.tres variant-literal parser (int vectors, Vector4/Quaternion/Plane/AABB/Basis/Projection, StringName, typed arrays) and surface parse errors
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/tscn-parser] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot's VariantParser reads every math literal and preserves types exactly. Patina's parse_variant_value (gdresource/loader.rs:232+) coerces Vector2i/Vector3i to float vectors and cannot parse Vector4(i), Quaternion, Plane, AABB, Basis, Projection, StringName (&"..."), typed Array[T]([...]), or Object(...); packed_scene.rs then silently discards unparseable properties. Add the missing literal arms (mapping to the correct gdvariant types — requires Vector4/Quaternion/Plane/AABB/Projection Variant variants; add them if absent), preserve int-vector types, and change packed_scene.rs to propagate parse errors (or at minimum store the raw literal) instead of dropping the property.
acceptance_criteria: Parsing a .tscn node with position=Vector2i(3,4), basis-bearing transform=Transform3D(...), rot=Quaternion(0,0,0,1), and cells=PackedInt32Array(...) preserves the integer vector as an int type and round-trips the Transform3D/Quaternion values; a property with a genuinely malformed value produces a reported error rather than being silently missing. (test: `tscn_parses_intvec_and_math_literals`)

title: GDScript: expose ProjectSettings, ResourceSaver, ResourceUID, Marshalls singletons + var_to_bytes/str_to_var utilities
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/io-singletons] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

title: Image import: decode WebP source + WebP-compressed .ctex (Godot default web/2D texture)
description:
[audit-key: image-import-format-breadth-webp-svg-compressed/image-decode-webp] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: WebP is decoded by Image.load_webp_from_buffer (doc/classes/Image.xml:423) via modules/webp/image_loader_webp.cpp (registered by default, register_types.cpp:45). The default texture importer (editor/import/resource_importer_texture.cpp:234, PRESET default 0=Lossless) stores imported 2D textures as WebP inside .ctex with inner DATA_FORMAT_WEBP=2 — so opening ANY real imported/exported project routes imported PNG/JPG/etc. through a WebP-in-.ctex artifact. Patina current state: no WebP decoder exists in the workspace (gdresource/Cargo.toml has only miniz_oxide; grep for decode_webp/load_webp/image-webp/libwebp across crates/ is empty). ctex.rs:152-154 returns EngineError::Unsupported('no WebP decoder in this build') for DATA_FORMAT_WEBP, and importers.rs::ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults (importers.rs:579) registers no `.webp` extension, so source .webp also cannot load. Implementation: add a pure-Rust WebP decoder dep (e.g. `image` with `webp` feature, or `image-webp`) to gdresource/Cargo.toml; add `decode_webp_bytes -> (w,h,format,pixels)` and (a) branch ctex.rs's DATA_FORMAT_WEBP to decode the embedded WebP level-0 payload into the same Texture2D Resource shape build_raw_texture/import_image_bytes produce, and (b) register `.webp` in ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults dispatching to a new import_webp producing a pixel-bearing Texture2D. Wiring requirement: ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults().load_resource(path) must decode both a loose `.webp` and a `.import`→`.ctex(WebP)` artifact (via resolve_import_artifact, importers.rs:62) end-to-end to a Texture2D whose `pixels` Variant::Array is populated — identical contract to the existing PNG path.
acceptance_criteria: ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults().load_resource('foo.webp') returns class Texture2D with a non-empty `pixels` array of the correct dimensions/colors; and load_resource on a .ctex whose inner data_format is DATA_FORMAT_WEBP (2) returns decoded pixels instead of an Unsupported error; and a source PNG with a `.import` sidecar redirecting to a WebP `.ctex` loads real pixels. (test: `webp_import_wiring`)

title: FileAccess: typed get/store (8-64/half/float/double/real/var/line/csv/pascal), endianness, compressed + encrypted modes, md5/sha
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/file-access] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Games use FileAccess for save files with typed binary reads/writes, big-endian control, compression, encryption, and hashing. gdcore/file_access.rs currently only does whole-buffer/string read/write. Implement the typed get_*/store_* family (little/big-endian aware via a big_endian flag), get_var/store_var using the binary Variant codec, get_line/get_csv_line/get_pascal_string, open_compressed (fastlz/deflate/zstd/gzip via miniz_oxide + a fastlz impl), open_encrypted(+with_pass) using gdcore::crypto AES, and get_md5/get_sha256. Expose them all through the interpreter FileAccess instance dispatch. Note the wasm user:// backend (IndexedDB/OPFS) as a follow-up so the API is web-usable.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript writes a save file with store_32/store_float/store_var, closes, reopens, and get_32/get_float/get_var read back the exact values; toggling set_big_endian(true) changes the on-disk byte order; open_compressed round-trips a buffer. (test: `file_access_typed_binary_roundtrip`)

title: Image: implement the Godot Image class (pixel API, formats, mipmaps, resize, blit/blend, load/save buffers) + ImageTexture, register + script-expose
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/image] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Image is one of the most-used data classes and is entirely absent — only scattered PNG decoders exist. Create a gdresource (or gdcore) Image type holding width/height/Format/data with the core API: create/create_empty/create_from_data, get/set_pixel(v), get_format/convert (across the L8/RGBA8/RF/RGBAF/RGBE families), get_data/get_data_size, generate_mipmaps/get_mipmap_offset, resize/crop/shrink_x2, blit_rect(+mask)/blend_rect(+mask), fill(_rect), get_used_rect/get_region, flip_x/flip_y, load_png_from_buffer/load_jpg_from_buffer + save_png(_to_buffer). title: Resources: wire PCK mount + binary .scn/.res loading into the boot path (RSCC, full variant decode, binary PackedScene)
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/binary-pck] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

A real Godot web export ships a .pck of binary .scn/.res files fetched over HTTP. Patina has a complete PCK reader (pck.rs) and a partial binary .res reader (res_loader.rs) but nothing mounts a PCK or reads binary resources at boot, and there is no binary PackedScene loader. Wire a PCK mount into patina-runner boot (fetch/read bytes → PckMountManager → res:// resolves inside the pack), extend res_loader.rs to handle RSCC compression, big-endian, and the full variant set (packed arrays + objects), and add a binary PackedScene decoder that reconstructs the node-path-indexed tree. Route ResourceLoader through the mounted pack.
acceptance_criteria: Given a .pck built by PckPacker containing a binary .scn main scene, the runner mounts it and boots the scene into the tree (node count/names match the source), proving the fetch→PCK→binary-resource→scene-tree chain end to end. (test: `runner_boots_binary_scene_from_pck`)

title: SceneTree/Viewport: dispatch _input/_unhandled_input/_shortcut_input/_unhandled_key_input with push_input + set_input_as_handled
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/input-propagation] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot routes each InputEvent through Viewport::push_input in a fixed order: _input (tree order) → GUI/gui_input (focus + mouse target) → _shortcut_input → _unhandled_key_input → _unhandled_input → physics picking, with set_input_as_handled() short-circuiting later stages (viewport.cpp). Nodes opt in via set_process_input/set_process_unhandled_input/etc. Patina has none of this: MainLoop::step (main_loop.rs:344) only builds a polling InputSnapshot; there is no process_script_input path (scene_tree.rs:1465-1493 lists only ready/process/physics/enter/exit) and no set_input_as_handled. Implement SceneTree::push_input(event) that walks nodes in Godot stage order, invokes the corresponding script virtual on nodes that enabled it, honors a per-event input_handled flag, and is called from MainLoop::step for each queued InputEvent BEFORE the process phase. Add process_script_input / process_script_unhandled_input dispatch to the gdscene scripting bridge plus per-node input-enable flags, and route the editor key/mouse endpoints (editor_server.rs:10106) through push_input rather than only InputState.
acceptance_criteria: A scene whose script implements _unhandled_input(event) and sets a var flips that var when a key InputEvent is pushed and MainLoop::step runs; a node that calls set_input_as_handled() in _input prevents a sibling's _unhandled_input from seeing the same event. (test: unhandled_input_dispatched_via_main_loop)

title: SceneTree/Node: emit lifecycle + per-frame signals (process_frame, physics_frame, node_added, tree_entered, …)
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/tree-signals] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot emits SceneTree.process_frame/physics_frame each frame (immediately before _process/_physics_process) and tree-mutation signals tree_changed/node_added/node_removed/node_renamed/tree_process_mode_changed/scene_changed; Nodes emit tree_entered/tree_exiting/tree_exited/child_entered_tree/child_exiting_tree/child_order_changed/ready/renamed. Scripts routinely `await get_tree().process_frame` and `node.tree_exiting.connect(...)`. Patina emits none: MainLoop::step (main_loop.rs) has no process_frame/physics_frame emission, and add_child/remove_node/reparent/set_name + LifecycleManager (lifecycle.rs) only append notifications to the log — no signal fires. Emit these through the existing SceneTree signal store (scene_tree.rs:1102 emit_signal): emit tree-level signals inside MainLoop::step (process_frame before the process phase, physics_frame before each physics tick) and inside add_child/remove_node/reparent/set_name; emit the Node-level signals on the affected node during enter/exit/child-order transitions in LifecycleManager.
acceptance_criteria: A script connecting to get_tree().process_frame AND to a child node's tree_entered receives both callbacks when the scene is stepped once through MainLoop; node_added fires when add_child inserts a live node and node_renamed fires on set_name. (test: scene_tree_and_node_signals_fire_via_main_loop)

title: SceneTree: change_scene_to_file, unload_current_scene, quit + auto_accept_quit/quit_on_go_back, get_frame, physics_interpolation
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scenetree-scene-api] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot's most-used scene API is change_scene_to_file(path) — deferred: free current scene, load+instance the .tscn, set current_scene — plus unload_current_scene, quit(exit_code) with auto_accept_quit/quit_on_go_back semantics, get_frame() (Engine frame counter), get_processed_tweens(), and physics_interpolation toggle (scene_tree.cpp). Patina has only change_scene_to_packed/_to_node/reload (scene_tree.rs:1806-1900). Implement change_scene_to_file by loading the res:// path through the existing PackedScene loader and delegating to change_scene_to_packed with Godot's deferred timing (swap at end of frame); add unload_current_scene, a quit() path that signals the MainLoop/PlatformBackend to stop (and the editor to Stop), get_frame() returning MainLoop.frame_count, get_processed_tweens(), and a physics_interpolation flag surfaced to the renderer. Wire change_scene_to_file so a script calling get_tree().change_scene_to_file('res://next.tscn') actually swaps the running scene in patina-runner and editor Play.
acceptance_criteria: Stepping a scene whose script calls change_scene_to_file('res://b.tscn') replaces current_scene with b's root by the next frame; quit() ends patina-runner's run loop (should_quit becomes true). (test: change_scene_to_file_swaps_running_scene)

title: Node: add_sibling, wildcard find_child/find_children/find_parent, has_node, get_path_to, is_ancestor_of, propagate_call/notification
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/node-query-api] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot's Node query surface (node.cpp) includes add_sibling(node, force_readable_name), find_child(pattern, recursive, owned) and find_children(pattern, type, recursive, owned) with String wildcard matching, find_parent(pattern), has_node(path), get_path_to(node), is_ancestor_of(node), and propagate_notification(what)/propagate_call(method, args, parent_first). Patina exposes only exact-path resolution (scene_tree.rs get_node_by_path:695, find_child_by_name:711) plus get_index/node_path; the wildcard find_child/find_children, add_sibling, find_parent, get_path_to, is_ancestor_of and propagate_* are absent (0 non-test hits). Implement these on SceneTree over NodeId with Godot wildcard semantics (`*`/`?`), add_sibling inserting immediately after the node in its parent's child list (with unique-name resolution), and propagate_call/notification walking the subtree parent-first/child order. Expose them to the GDScript bridge so scripts can call node.find_child('Enemy*') and node.add_sibling(n).
acceptance_criteria: On a loaded scene, find_children('*', 'Sprite2D', true) returns every Sprite2D descendant, find_child('Ene*') matches by wildcard, add_sibling inserts a node immediately after its sibling in tree order, and propagate_call reaches all descendants. (test: node_find_and_sibling_queries)

title: SceneTree: make root a Window/Viewport with get_viewport/get_window and content-scale stretch pipeline
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/viewport-tree] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

In Godot the SceneTree root is a Window (subclass of Viewport); every Node.get_viewport()/get_window() climbs to it, and its content_scale_mode (disabled/canvas_items/viewport) + content_scale_aspect (ignore/keep/keep_width/keep_height/expand) + content_scale_factor drive the stretch transform applied to the whole canvas (window.cpp — the web-canvas resize path). Patina creates the root as a bare Node (scene_tree.rs:114) with no Viewport/Window semantics, no get_viewport/get_window, no world_2d/world_3d, and content-scale only stored as an unused project-settings string (project_settings_dialog.rs:566). Make the root a Window-class node carrying Viewport state (size, world_2d/world_3d, canvas_transform), implement Node.get_viewport()/get_window() returning it, parse display/window/stretch/{mode,aspect,scale} from project.godot, and compute+apply the content-scale transform into the 2D draw path (gdrender2d) for both patina-runner and editor Play/viewport.
acceptance_criteria: get_viewport() on any node returns the root Window; with stretch mode=canvas_items, aspect=keep and a base size, rendering a scene into a 2x window scales the emitted canvas transform / draw output by 2. (test: root_window_content_scale_stretch)

title: Shaders: uniform hints + global/instance uniforms + ShaderInclude #include preprocessor
description:
[audit-key: shaders/shader-uniforms-globals-include] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: uniform hints drive semantics (source_color sRGB decode, hint_range clamps + inspector slider, filter_*/repeat_* sampler state, screen_texture/depth_texture/normal_roughness_texture bind engine buffers); `global uniform` values are stored in ProjectSettings shader_globals and set at runtime via RenderingServer.global_shader_parameter_set; `instance uniform` are per-instance overrides; ShaderInclude (.gdshaderinc) + `#include` compose sources (doc/classes/Shader.xml, ShaderInclude.xml). Patina current state: hints are opaque strings with no behavior (gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:65); no global parameter store; RenderingServer.global_shader_parameter_* unimplemented; #include/ShaderInclude absent; instance/global uniforms lexed but ignored. Implementation approach: parse the full hint grammar and apply hint semantics in the compiler/interpreter; add a global-shader-parameter registry (seeded from project.godot shader_globals, mutable via a RenderingServer surface) and resolve `global uniform` reads from it; resolve `#include`/ShaderInclude during compilation (register a .gdshaderinc loader in gdresource/importers.rs). Wiring requirement: setting a global uniform at runtime changes shaded output next frame, and a #include'd function is callable in the fragment body.
acceptance_criteria: A shader declaring `global uniform vec4 sky_tint;` renders using the value set via the global-parameter API (changing it changes output), a `source_color` hinted uniform is sRGB-decoded, and a `#include "res://lib.gdshaderinc"` function resolves and executes. (test: `shader_uniform_hints_and_globals`)

title: Theme: full default theme (55 control types), icon item type, type variations, and Control get/add_theme_* resolution API
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/theme-system] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: STUB]

Godot's Theme (api: 69 methods) stores 6 item types (color/constant/font/font_size/icon/stylebox) with type variations and base types; default_theme.cpp generates the built-in theme with 794 item assignments across 55 control types; Controls resolve theme items by walking the theme_owner parent chain and merging per-instance overrides via ~40 Control methods (get_theme_color, add_theme_stylebox_override, has_theme_font, get_theme_default_font, set_theme_type_variation, begin/end_bulk_theme_override). Patina's Theme (gdscene/src/theme.rs) is a 5-category HashMap with no Icon type, styleboxes stored as flat Variant::Color, and a default_theme() covering only Label/Button/Panel (theme.rs:186); Control has no theme-resolution API at all (grep for get_theme_color/add_theme_*_override finds nothing); nothing is registered in gdobject/src/class_db.rs. Implementation: extend gdscene/src/theme.rs with an Icon item type, type variations/base types, default font/size, merge/clear, and a get_theme_*/has_theme_*/add_theme_*_override resolution that walks the node's theme_owner chain (gdscene/src/control.rs); port default_theme.cpp coverage for the full control-type set; register Theme+ThemeDB in class_db.rs so .tscn/[gd_resource type="Theme"] loads into a usable Theme. Wiring requirement: a Control in a scene with a custom Theme and an add_theme_color_override resolves the override, then the theme, then ThemeDB default - and that resolved value feeds the render path from the text-render-wiring bead.
acceptance_criteria: A scene with a Button that has a theme_type_variation and an add_theme_color_override('font_color') resolves font_color from the override; removing it falls back to the assigned Theme, then to the default theme; the default theme exposes styleboxes/colors/constants for the full Godot control-type set (Label, Button, Panel, LineEdit, Tree, ... ) and Theme/ThemeDB are constructible via ClassDB. (test: `control_theme_override_resolution`)

title: Input singleton: add get_axis / is_action_just_released / get_action_strength + capture just_released in the snapshot + circular-deadzone get_vector/get_axis
description:
[audit-key: input/input-singleton-api] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]
[verify-note: ADJUSTED: All technical claims verified: call_input_method (interpreter.rs:3167-3287) handles exactly 6 methods (is_action_pressed/is_action_just_pressed/is_key_pressed/get_global_mouse_position/is_mouse_button_pressed/get_vector) with `other => UndefinedFunction` catch-all (3284); Input.* routes ON]

Godot ground truth (core/input/input.cpp): Input.get_axis(neg,pos)=strength(pos)-strength(neg); get_vector applies the max action deadzone to the raw vector length then renormalizes (circular deadzone); is_action_just_released mirrors just_pressed; get_action_strength/raw return analog magnitude (raw ignores deadzone). Patina current: interpreter call_input_method (gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:3167) has only 6 methods — get_axis, is_action_just_released, get_action_strength, get_mouse_position, is_physical_key_pressed are absent; the script InputSnapshot (gdscene/src/scripting.rs:167) carries no just_released_keys at all, and get_vector (gdplatform/src/input.rs:738) ignores deadzone. Approach: add a just_released_keys HashSet to gdscene InputSnapshot and populate it from InputState (flush pipeline already tracks keys_just_released); add SceneAccess methods get_input_axis, is_input_action_just_released, get_action_strength; register the corresponding names in call_input_method; port Godot's circular-deadzone get_vector/get_axis into InputState/InputSnapshot. Wiring requirement: a GDScript calling Input.get_axis(), Input.is_action_just_released(), Input.get_action_strength() during _process in a running scene returns correct values (not an error) through the editor Play snapshot bridge (editor_server.rs make_input_snapshot -> main_loop.set_input).
acceptance_criteria: A scene script that in _process records Input.get_axis("ui_left","ui_right"), Input.is_action_just_released("ui_accept"), and Input.get_action_strength("ui_right") returns -1/0/1 for get_axis across press/both/release frames, true on the exact frame ui_accept is released (and false the next), and 1.0 strength while held — with a diagonal get_vector normalized after deadzone (test: `input_singleton_polling_e2e`).

title: StyleBox: StyleBoxFlat/Texture/Line/Empty resources + bordered/rounded/nine-patch drawing wired into Control rendering
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/stylebox] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot draws Control backgrounds via StyleBox resources: StyleBoxFlat (bg_color, per-side border_width + border_color, per-corner corner_radius + corner_detail, expand_margin_*, content margins, shadow_color/size/offset, skew, anti_aliasing - 23 properties), StyleBoxTexture (nine-patch with per-axis stretch/tile/tile-fit + modulate + region), StyleBoxLine, StyleBoxEmpty (scene/resources/style_box_flat.cpp etc.). Patina has no runtime StyleBox class - none registered in gdobject/src/class_db.rs, styleboxes are stored as flat Variant::Color in gdscene/src/theme.rs:209, and nothing draws borders/corners/shadows (control.rs:1024-1059 only stores theme_override_styles/* as Variants; gdeditor/src/theme_editor.rs:85 is editor-only data). Implementation: add StyleBox resource types (gdscene or gdrender2d) parsed from .tscn/.tres sub_resources, register them in class_db.rs, and add a draw_stylebox routine in gdrender2d (rounded-rect fill + per-side borders + shadow + AA; nine-patch for StyleBoxTexture reusing draw::draw_nine_patch); consume the theme's stylebox item when rendering Panel/Button/Control backgrounds. Wiring requirement: a Panel/Button in a scene whose theme has a StyleBoxFlat renders a bordered, corner-rounded background to the framebuffer.
acceptance_criteria: A scene with a Panel using a StyleBoxFlat (bg_color, border_width>0, corner_radius>0) renders a background with the fill color inside, a distinct border color on the edges, and rounded (non-square) corners; a Button with a StyleBoxTexture renders its nine-patch stretch regions. (test: `stylebox_flat_draws_borders_and_corners`)

title: TextServer: line breaking, autowrap, alignment, ellipsis, tab stops via TextParagraph/TextLine layout
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/textserver-layout] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: STUB]

Godot lays out text through TextServer + TextParagraph/TextLine: breaking lines by word/grapheme/CJK against a width, applying autowrap_mode, horizontal/vertical alignment, justification_flags, text_overrun_behavior (ellipsis/trim), and tab stops, with per-size glyph metrics (ascent/descent/advance) (servers/text/text_server.cpp; scene/resources/text_paragraph.cpp). Patina's TextServerLite (gdrender2d/src/text_server.rs) only returns a fixed per-char advance (2 methods vs 236); TextLine/TextParagraph do not exist; Label's stored autowrap_mode/horizontal_alignment (gdscene/src/control.rs:800-843) drive nothing (no layout consumer); draw_string_multiline wraps only on literal newlines (font.rs:568). Implementation: build a TextParagraph/TextLine layout module in gdrender2d that, given a string + font (from the font-stack bead) + width + alignment + wrap mode + overrun behavior, produces positioned glyph runs (line breaks, alignment offsets, ellipsis); expose glyph metrics per size on the TextServer; have the Label update path (text-render-wiring bead) request a paragraph layout and emit one DrawString per positioned run. Wiring requirement: a Label with autowrap enabled and a bounded width wraps its text across multiple lines with the chosen alignment when rendered.
acceptance_criteria: A Label with a fixed width, autowrap_mode=word and horizontal_alignment=right, given text longer than its width, renders on multiple lines each right-aligned within the rect; text_overrun_behavior=trim_ellipsis on a single-line Label produces a trailing ellipsis; tab characters advance to tab stops. (test: `label_autowrap_and_alignment_layout`)

title: i18n: TranslationServer singleton + tr()/tr_n() builtins + .po/.csv loaders + auto_translate re-render
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/i18n] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot's TranslationServer (core/string/translation_server.cpp, 35 methods) matches locales (with script/country fallback + plural rules), holds Translation catalogs loaded from .po (context + plurals) and .csv, and Object.tr()/tr_n() look up the active-locale string; auto_translate_mode makes Controls re-translate their text on locale change; pseudolocalization + number formatting round out the surface. Patina has none: no TranslationServer/Translation impl or registration (grep empty), no tr/tr_n GDScript builtin (gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs has print/str/load but no tr), no .po/.csv importer, and auto_translate_mode is an inert inspector property (gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:27). Implementation: add a TranslationServer singleton (gdcore or gdscene) with add_translation/set_locale/translate/translate_plural + locale fallback; add .po and .csv translation loaders (gdresource/src/importers.rs / loader) producing Translation resources; add tr()/tr_n() as Object methods routed by the GDScript interpreter (gdscript-interop) and script-reachable TranslationServer; propagate auto_translate so a Label re-renders on locale change. Wiring requirement: a script in a scene calling tr("KEY") after set_locale returns the catalog value and the bound Label re-renders the translated text via the text-render pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .po catalog with an entry KEY->"Bonjour", calling TranslationServer.set_locale('fr') then tr('KEY') from a GDScript in a scene returns 'Bonjour'; a Label with auto_translate whose text is 'KEY' shows the translated string, and switching locale re-renders it; tr_n selects the correct plural form. (test: `tr_translates_via_po_catalog`)

title: ParticleProcessMaterial: register resource class and parse its full property set from .tscn/.tres
description:
[audit-key: vfx-particles/particle-process-material] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: ParticleProcessMaterial is the resource that drives GPU particles; it exposes ~120 properties and 4 enums (EmissionShape POINT/SPHERE/SPHERE_SURFACE/BOX/POINTS/DIRECTED_POINTS/RING, ParticleFlags, SubEmitterMode, CollisionMode) plus min/max + CurveTexture curve for every parameter (scene/resources/particle_process_material.cpp). A .tscn references it as `process_material = SubResource("ParticleProcessMaterial_...")`. Patina current state: the class is unregistered (unregistered.txt; class_db.rs has no entry) and gdresource has no parse path (grep empty), so the process_material is silently dropped; particle nodes fall back to ad-hoc inline material structs (gdscene/src/particle.rs:87, gdserver3d/src/particles3d.rs:110). Implementation approach: (1) register ParticleProcessMaterial (parent Material) in gdobject/src/class_db.rs with its property + enum list; (2) parse the resource from text .tscn/.tres sub-resources in gdresource (loader.rs) into a Rust struct holding the full parameter set (emission shape+params, direction/spread/flatness, gravity, per-param min/max, curves, color/color_ramp, flags, collision/sub_emitter/turbulence groups); (3) hand that struct to the particle node's simulator (the wiring bead) replacing the inline material. Wiring requirement: scene load parses the SubResource -> node.process_material is populated -> simulator reads real values (start this with emission shape + gravity + initial velocity so it is observable).
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn whose GPUParticles2D/3D has a ParticleProcessMaterial SubResource (with e.g. emission_shape=BOX, gravity, initial_velocity_min/max, spread) results in a node whose simulator uses those exact values — particles emit within the box extents and integrate under the parsed gravity — verified by inspecting frame output after scene load (not by constructing the material in Rust). (test: `particle_process_material_parses_from_tscn`)

title: Web runtime: wasm32 cdylib entry + browser boot + rAF fixed-timestep MainLoop driver
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web_wasm_runtime] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

A browser-native engine must actually run in the browser. Godot's web platform (web_main.cpp) provides an emscripten entry that acquires the canvas, initializes the GL/WebGL2 (or WebGPU) context, and installs a main-loop callback driven by the browser; engine.js/preloader.js handle async load + progress. Patina has none of this: no wasm target, no wasm-bindgen/cdylib, and patina-runner (main.rs) is a native JSON-dumping CLI with a for-loop over a fixed frame count — not a real-time rAF loop. Implementation (stage this): (1) add a wasm crate (crate-type=cdylib) with a wasm-bindgen start() entry that acquires the <canvas>, requests a WebGPU adapter/device with a WebGL2 fallback, and installs a panic hook routing to console.error + an on-screen overlay; (2) implement a fixed-timestep driver (accumulator) invoked from requestAnimationFrame that calls gdscene MainLoop::step at the physics tick rate with visibility-hidden throttling and max_fps honoring; (3) feed the existing renderer/scene-tree so a loaded PackedScene renders to the canvas. Factor the timestep accumulator so its logic is unit-testable on native. This is the foundational enabler for the rest of the web-runtime beads (export payload, JS bridge, browser input/audio, persistence).
acceptance_criteria: The engine builds for wasm32-unknown-unknown (verifier build check) with a wasm-bindgen entry point, and the fixed-timestep browser driver advances gdscene MainLoop deterministically: feeding N seconds of accumulated frame time produces the Godot-correct number of physics steps and advances a scripted _process counter. (test: `web_runtime_fixed_timestep_driver`) exercises the accumulator driving a real MainLoop over simulated elapsed time and asserts step count + a scene _process side effect, proving the driver is wired to the scene tick rather than to a fixed batch count.

comments.author: IvoryDune
comments.text:
AUTO-CLOSED BUT THE BROWSER HALF IS NOT DONE -- a game still cannot run in a browser (IvoryDune 2026-07-16). Flagging because a CLOSED status here will overstate web-runtime parity on any scorecard.

DELIVERED: gdscene/src/frame_driver.rs -- FrameDriver turns requestAnimationFrame timestamps into MainLoop::step calls (delta from successive DOMHighResTimeStamps, 0.25s max_frame_delta clamp so a backgrounded tab resuming with a multi-second jump cannot spiral, max_fps coalescing, hidden-tab throttling; skipped callbacks CARRY their delta so N seconds of browser time still yields N seconds of engine time). Pure logic over an injected timestamp, no browser types -- exactly the "factor the accumulator so it is unit-testable on native" the bead asked for. Plus gdscene/tests/web_runtime_fixed_timestep_driver.rs (the named acceptance test): 1s as 60x16.6ms -> 60 steps / 60 physics ticks / _process=60, and the same second as 20x50ms -> 20 steps but STILL 60 physics ticks. Verify with: nextest run -p gdscene --test web_runtime_fixed_timestep_driver

Deliberately did NOT duplicate the physics accumulator: MainLoop::step already banks delta and runs fixed 1/physics_ticks_per_second ticks capped by max_physics_steps_per_frame. The driver owns only the browser-side concerns.

NOT DELIVERED -- suggest splitting into new beads:
 (1) wasm entry does not acquire the <canvas>, request a WebGPU adapter/device, or fall back to WebGL2
 (2) no requestAnimationFrame callback is installed, and no on-screen panic overlay (only console_error_panic_hook, inherited from pat-u3l8c.109)
 (3) nothing feeds the renderer -- a loaded PackedScene does not draw to the canvas
 (4) max_fps is a driver setting, not yet read from Engine.max_fps / ProjectSettings

WHY THE BROWSER HALF IS BLOCKED, NOT MERELY SKIPPED: patina-web cannot depend on gdscene today -- gdscene -> gdaudio -> cpal is an unconditional native dep that breaks the wasm32 build (which is why pat-u3l8c.109 deliberately scoped patina-web to gdcore+gdvariant only). Wiring FrameDriver into patina-web's rAF entry requires the cpal cfg-gating owned by the audio web bead (pat-u3l8c.112). The driver was therefore landed in gdscene, where MainLoop lives and where it is natively provable now; the follow-up is then pure glue over an already-tested accumulator.

title: Register AnimationNode* Resource classes and load AnimationTree graphs from .tres
description:
[audit-key: animation/animation/animation-node-tree-family] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL] [unverified]

acceptance_criteria: A .tres AnimationTree whose tree_root is an AnimationNodeBlendTree containing an Add2 node blending two AnimationNodeAnimation nodes loads and evaluates: setting the Add2 blend parameter mixes the two clips, and ClassDB reports the registered AnimationNode* parents. (test: `animation_tree_blendtree_add2_tres_loads_and_blends`)

title: Editor: serve Project Settings -> Autoload tab wired to AutoloadManager (CRUD + reorder + persist to project.godot)
description:
[audit-key: autoload-global-singletons-runtime/autoload-editor-ui] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

GODOT: the editor's Project Settings -> Autoload tab lets the user add/remove/rename/reorder/enable autoloads, persisting to the [autoload] section. PATINA: a complete model exists — gdeditor/src/autoload_manager.rs AutoloadManager (add/remove/rename/move_up/move_down/set_enabled/globals/to_cfg/from_cfg) — but it is UNWIRED: no editor_server.rs route references it, project_settings_dialog.rs has 0 autoload refs, and EDITOR_HTML (editor_ui.rs) never mentions autoload. IMPLEMENTATION: hold an AutoloadManager in EditorState loaded from project.godot [autoload] (from_cfg) at startup; add editor_server.rs routes — GET list, POST add/remove/reorder/toggle-enabled — that mutate the manager and write back to project.godot via to_cfg (order-preserving, matching the runtime declaration-order bead); add the Autoload tab UI to EDITOR_HTML (editor_ui.rs) and project_settings_dialog.rs that calls those routes and renders the ordered list with enable checkboxes and up/down controls. Guard the served JS by testing pub const EDITOR_HTML directly so the client actually calls the route.
acceptance_criteria: POSTing to the autoload-add route writes Global="*res://global.gd" into project.godot's [autoload] section and the served editor GET lists it in order; reorder/remove/toggle-enabled update both the AutoloadManager and the persisted file; EDITOR_HTML contains the Autoload tab markup that invokes the routes. (test: `editor_autoload_tab_crud_persists` — drive the editor server add/reorder/remove routes against a temp project and assert both the JSON responses and the rewritten project.godot [autoload] section)

comments.author: IvoryDune
comments.text:
AUTO-CLOSED BUT ONLY ~25% DELIVERED (IvoryDune 2026-07-16).

DELIVERED: gdeditor/src/autoload_manager.rs gains to_project_godot_section() / from_project_godot_section() = REAL project.godot [autoload] INI (Name="*path", the * marks enabled exactly as Godot's Enable checkbox does, declaration-order preserving, reads only [autoload] out of a full project file) + 4 unit tests. Verify with: nextest run -p gdeditor --lib autoload_manager

WHY THAT WAS NEEDED: this bead's own plan said "persist via to_cfg", but to_cfg() is serde_json::to_string_pretty(self) -- it emits JSON despite its doc comment claiming "Serializes the [autoload] section to project-settings text". Following the bead literally would write a JSON blob into project.godot where an INI section belongs, and the acceptance (Global="*res://global.gd" present in the file) could never pass. The to_cfg/from_cfg docs are now corrected to say plainly they are JSON state snapshots, not project.godot text.

NOT DELIVERED -- suggest splitting into new beads:
 (1) hold an AutoloadManager in EditorState, loaded via from_project_godot_section at startup
 (2) editor_server.rs routes: GET list, POST add/remove/reorder/toggle-enabled, each rewriting project.godot
 (3) Autoload tab markup in EDITOR_HTML (editor_ui.rs) + project_settings_dialog.rs, guarded by an EDITOR_HTML-string test so the served JS actually calls the routes
 (4) the named acceptance test editor_autoload_tab_crud_persists

Scoped out deliberately, not overlooked: editor_server.rs is 21k lines and carries uncommitted concurrent work; a half-applied edit there breaks gdeditor for every worker in the swarm. The foundation landed above is what those routes call, so (1)-(4) are now purely additive.

SEPARATE BUG -- needs its own gdresource bead: ProjectLoader::get_autoloads (gdresource/src/project.rs ~331) ends with entries.sort_by(|a,b| a.name.cmp(&b.name)) "Sort by name for deterministic order". Godot uses DECLARATION order, and that order IS load order (an autoload may reference one declared before it). Patina therefore boots autoloads alphabetically, silently reordering _ready for any project whose declaration order is not alphabetical -- breaking the exact cross-autoload reference that pat-nzgdu.3 / pat-nzgdu.70 exist to support. Left untouched here: wrong crate for this bead, shared code, and existing tests may encode the sorted order.

title: ClassDB: expose script singleton + add signals/constants/enums to ClassInfo + instance reflection
description:
[audit-key: core-object/core-object-classdb] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot ground truth: ClassDB is a global singleton scripts call (ClassDB.class_exists, get_parent_class, get_inheriters_from_class, can_instantiate, instantiate, class_has_method, class_get_method_list, class_has_signal, class_get_signal_list, class_get_integer_constant(_list), class_has_enum/class_get_enum_list/class_get_enum_constants, class_get_property_list); and every Object answers has_method/has_signal/get_method_list/get_signal_list/get_property_list/get_instance_id. Patina current state: ClassInfo (class_db.rs:64-83) stores only properties+methods (no signals/constants/enums); PropertyInfo/MethodInfo are thin (class_db.rs:17-52); nothing exposes ClassDB or instance reflection to GDScript (grep 0). Implementation: extend ClassInfo/ClassRegistration with signals (name+arg schema), integer constants, and enums, and populate them in the register_*_classes tables; enrich PropertyInfo with type/usage/hint_string and MethodInfo with return/arg types; add a ClassDB singleton path in the interpreter that routes to gdobject::class_db; add SceneAccess reflection entry points (has_method/has_signal/get_method_list/get_signal_list/get_property_list/get_instance_id) implemented against ClassDB + the node. Wiring requirement: a script must query ClassDB and its own class metadata and get non-empty, correct results.
acceptance_criteria: A script runs `assert(ClassDB.class_exists("Sprite2D")); assert(ClassDB.get_parent_class("Sprite2D") == "Node2D"); assert(ClassDB.class_has_method("Node","get_parent")); assert(has_method("_ready")); assert(get_method_list().size() > 0)` with no UndefinedFunction, and class_get_signal_list("Node") returns a non-empty list. (test: `classdb_singleton_reflection_test`) runnable via cargo nextest --test classdb_singleton_reflection_test.

comments.author: RedTower
comments.text: Triage (RedTower, no-run analysis): the gdobject-local foundation is a clean ADDITIVE slice — extend ClassInfo + ClassRegistration with signals/integer_constants/enums (default-empty fields; ONLY ONE ClassInfo{} construction site at class_db.rs:155 to update), add builder methods + inherited query fns (class_has_signal/class_get_signal_list/class_get_integer_constant/class_get_enum_list mirroring get_property_list), populate a few signals on Node. The bead's ACCEPTANCE (classdb_singleton_reflection_test) is GDScript-driven, so it additionally needs the cross-crate interpreter part: a ClassDB singleton path in gdscript-interop + SceneAccess reflection entry points (has_method/has_signal/get_method_list/get_signal_list/get_property_list/get_instance_id). Left unclaimed by a no-cargo worker because the acceptance can't pass without the interpreter binding; a cargo-capable worker should take the whole thing.

comments.author: GentleBadger
comments.text: PARTIAL by GentleBadger (2026-07-16, uncommitted; verify cmds in completion mail msg 53946). Followed RedTower's triage. DONE (2 crates, additive): gdobject/src/class_db.rs — SignalInfo{name,arguments} + EnumInfo{name,constants}; ClassInfo/ClassRegistration gain signals/integer_constants/enums (DEFAULT-EMPTY so all existing registrations are unaffected); builders .signal()/.constant()/.enumeration() (enum constants also register as integer constants, as Godot does); inherited query fns get_signal_list/class_has_signal/get_integer_constant_list/class_get_integer_constant/get_enum_list/class_has_enum/get_enum_constants (base-first like get_property_list; derived-first shadowing for constant lookup). Object/Node now carry their real method surface (incl. get_parent), signals, NOTIFICATION_* constants (sourced from crate::notification, NOT hardcoded) and Node's ProcessMode/InternalMode/DuplicateFlags enums. gdobject/src/lib.rs re-exports the new surface. gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs — extended the EXISTING ClassDB singleton with get_parent_class/class_has_signal/class_get_signal_list/class_get_integer_constant(+_list)/class_has_enum/class_get_enum_list/class_get_enum_constants. 16 tests. NOT COMPILED by me (worker build policy) — eye-verified + reviewer regression sweep. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD: (1) 'nothing exposes ClassDB to GDScript (grep 0)' is FALSE — a ClassDB singleton already existed (call_classdb_static, from pat-u3l8c.21) with class_exists/can_instantiate/class_has_method/get_class_list; I extended it. (2) Found+fixed a registration-ORDER bug: 6 register_*_classes entry points each bootstrap Object/Node behind a class_exists guard, so whichever ran first defined the metadata — both now come from shared object_class()/node_class() constructors (test pins order-independence). KEEP OPEN — REMAINING: (1) INSTANCE reflection has_method/get_method_list/get_signal_list/get_property_list/get_instance_id on self via SceneAccess — this BLOCKS the acceptance (Godot's has_method sees script-defined methods, so ClassDB alone cannot answer it); (2) the acceptance test classdb_singleton_reflection_test DOES NOT EXIST yet — do not trust a stale-recovery close (0-match filters exit 0); (3) ClassDB.class_get_method_list/class_get_property_list omitted deliberately — Godot returns richly-shaped dicts but MethodInfo only has name+arg_count; (4) richer PropertyInfo type/usage/hint_string + MethodInfo return/arg types; (5) signals populated on Object/Node only. NOTE for a possible separate bead: this tree's notification codes (PROCESS=17, PHYSICS_PROCESS=18, CHILD_ORDER_CHANGED=16) were NOT verified against Godot 4.6.1; ClassDB now sources them from crate::notification so there is a single source of truth either way.

comments.text: RESUBMIT after verifier FAIL (100, panic) — GentleBadger 2026-07-16, mail 54001. THE FAIL WAS NOT MY REGRESSION: 'class_db::tests::xr_nodes_classdb_registered' panicked on assert is_parent_class("XRServer","Object") — a PRE-EXISTING broken test that my deliberately-broad '--lib class_db' filter ran for the first time (earlier gdobject verifies used narrow filters like '--lib missing' / '--lib zip::tests' that never matched it). My diff was 194 insertions / 0 deletions and touched neither that test nor register_3d_classes. REAL UNDERLYING BUG (now FIXED): register_3d_classes() never bootstrapped the Object/Node roots, unlike the other 5 register_*_classes. It registers Node3D with parent 'Node' and XRServer with parent 'Object', but inheritance_chain only pushes classes it can FIND — so run on its own, that pass severed EVERY 3D class from the root: is_parent_class("Node3D","Node") and is_parent_class("XRServer","Object") were both FALSE. The XR test was just the only one asserting it. Fix: register_3d_classes now bootstraps Object/Node via the shared object_class()/node_class() constructors behind the same class_exists guard; added regression test register_3d_classes_alone_reaches_the_object_root; added '3d' to the order-independence test. VERIFIED SAFE FOR COUNT-SENSITIVE TESTS: node3d_runtime_slice_test (class_count()==12) pre-registers Object/Node in its own setup() so the guards skip and its custom Node (with 'name' property) is preserved; classdb_parity_test's all_17_classes_recognized uses its own register_core_classes() and never calls register_3d_classes, while high_use_runtime_classes_registered calls 3d AND 2d so the class SET is unchanged; the inline count tests (class_count_tracks, register_same_class_twice_overwrites) and the weakref fuzz test register manually. Only negative assertion !class_exists("Node") is in register_and_lookup, which doesn't call register_3d_classes. Keeping the BROAD filter deliberately — narrowing it to dodge the failure would hide a real defect.

title: RefCounted: attach RefCountedBase to script RefCounted/Resource instances so ref counting + auto-free work
description:
[audit-key: core-object/core-object-refcounted] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot ground truth: RefCounted.new() starts at refcount 1; sharing a reference increments and dropping decrements via reference()/unreference(); reaching 0 frees the object; get_reference_count() is script-observable; init_ref sets up first ownership. Patina current state: RefCountedBase (ref_counted.rs) is a correct-but-orphan primitive — 0 call sites outside gdobject (workspace grep) and no init_ref; script-created RefCounted objects therefore never count references or free. Implementation: give each script-instantiated RefCounted/Resource an owned RefCountedBase; increment/decrement it as the interpreter copies/drops Variant references that hold such objects; expose reference()/unreference()/get_reference_count()/init_ref() through the ObjectId (or Resource) dispatch and SceneAccess; free the backing object (and clear it from the alive registry) when the count hits 0. Also promote the WeakRef alive registry off thread_local so validity is process-global. Wiring requirement: RefCounted.new() in a script yields count 1 and its get_reference_count reflects additional references.
acceptance_criteria: A script executes `var r = RefCounted.new(); assert(r.get_reference_count() == 1); var r2 = r; assert(r.get_reference_count() == 2)` (or the engine's reference model) with no UndefinedFunction, and dropping all references invalidates a weakref taken to it. (test: `refcounted_reference_lifecycle_test`) runnable via cargo nextest --test refcounted_reference_lifecycle_test.

title: Editor: Import dock + asset import pipeline wired into FileSystem
description: No Import tab / reimport UI. Wire the import pipeline (glTF, PNG/JPEG/WebP, WAV/OGG, fonts) into the FileSystem dock with an Import settings panel and reimport-on-change. Acceptance: dropping a PNG into the project produces a usable Texture2D with import settings; covers fs_dock_import_hooks live.
close_reason: Import pipeline acceptance met: dropping a PNG into the project produces a usable Texture2D with import settings; fs_dock_import_hooks live (pat-oepf7). The import pipeline is wired into the FileSystem dock: the Import tab (#import-dock with an 'Import As:' select) populated via renderImportDock; GET /api/import_settings derives the importer from the extension (ImportResourceType::from_extension) -> a PNG reports importable=true, importer 'Texture2D', presets [Default, 2D Pixel, 2D, 3D] and 7 editable options (compression/filter/mipmaps/etc.), mirroring Godot's texture importer; POST /api/import_settings persists, POST /api/reimport reimports-on-change; and the texture decode path (TextureCache.get -> load_png -> gdrender2d::texture::decode_png, supporting RGBA + grayscale) turns a PNG into a usable Texture2D{width,height,pixels}. Added the named test fs_dock_import_hooks: /api/import_settings for a .png -> importable Texture2D with the 2D Pixel preset + compression/filter options; /api/reimport returns the path; a real PNG (encode_png of a 3x2 FrameBuffer) decode_png's back to a Texture2D with width 3/height 2 and the correct corner pixel; a .txt reports importable=false; the served dock wires /api/import_settings. Test PASS. Test-only change -> no regression risk. Chrome-verified on the running editor: the Import tab opens the dock (Import As: select present) and the served editor reads the PNG's real texture settings (Texture2D, 7 options, Godot presets). Source: upstream/godot/editor/import/resource_importer_texture.cpp + editor/import_dock.cpp.

FrameBuffer3D (renderer.rs:31) has set_pixel/set_depth with in-crate unit tests (:1949+). Shadow maps are CPU too (:424). So "decal projects albedo" / "fog volume density" is assertable in a PLAIN UNIT TEST on a framebuffer — no GPU, no editor, no viewport needed.

ADDITIVE-SAFE PLAN (breaks zero call sites — reflection_probes is the exact precedent):

Reconstruct each fragment's world pos from depth via inv_proj (apply_fog_pass already does exactly this — copy that reconstruction), map world->local per volume, sample_density, accumulate density and blend albedo + add emission.
  4. Call it from the two render entry points right next to the existing apply_fog_pass calls (:321 and :622).
  5. Tests in-crate: render a frame with a volume in front of the camera and assert the pixel shifts toward material.albedo; density=0 / volume outside the frustum leaves pixels unchanged; a point outside the shape contributes nothing (sample_density already returns 0.0 outside).

comments.author: GreenBadger
comments.text:
[GreenBadger 2026-07-16] CORRECTION to my previous comment + the real root cause of the Decal half.

I said earlier that Decal3D was "already fully implemented, just in the wrong crate". That was WRONG, and the truth is more important:

**gdscene/src/decal.rs IS DEAD CODE. It is never compiled.**
  - `grep -rn "mod decal" crates/` across the whole workspace = ZERO hits. The file is not declared by gdscene/src/lib.rs (which lists ~50 other `pub mod`s) nor by any other module.
  - Nothing anywhere references Decal3D / DecalRegistry (grep outside the file itself = zero hits).
  - It IS tracked/committed (df37e87 "Checkpoint: full engine, editor, 3D...") — so it was written, committed, and silently never wired in. 709 lines that have never been type-checked by rustc even once.

So the bead's premise ("Decal + FogVolume have math but are never called from renderer.rs/shader.rs") understates it for decals: the decal math is not merely uncalled, it is not part of any crate. Any "it's mostly done, just wire it" estimate is wrong.

Good news — it is probably close to compiling. It parses cleanly, and its entire external API surface is tiny and verified to exist: `use gdcore::math::{Color, Vector3}` + `use gdcore::math3d::Transform3D`; the only methods it calls are `.abs()` (37x), `Transform3D::xform` (2x), `Transform3D::inverse` (2x), `Color::WHITE`, `Vector3::new`. NOTHING gdscene-specific. That means it can move down the dependency graph with no import changes.

WHY IT MUST MOVE (unchanged from my last comment, and it is a hard constraint): the renderer is gdrender3d, and **gdscene depends on gdrender3d** (gdscene/Cargo.toml:19). gdrender3d can therefore never `use gdscene::decal` — dependency cycle, rejected by cargo. gdserver3d is where every other server-side render primitive lives (light.rs, reflection_probe.rs, fog_volume.rs) and gdrender3d already depends on it, and gdserver3d needs only gdcore — which is all decal.rs imports.

EXACT RECIPE for a builder-capable worker (should be quick):
  1. `git mv crates/gdscene/src/decal.rs crates/gdserver3d/src/decal.rs` — imports need NO change (gdcore only). Zero call sites to fix because there are zero callers.
  2. gdserver3d/src/lib.rs: add `pub mod decal;` (alphabetically after `csg`) + `pub use decal::{Decal3D, DecalRegistry, DecalTexture};` next to the fog_volume re-export on line 40. NOTE: this is the first time these 709 lines are ever compiled — expect to fix real rustc errors here. That is the actual work of this half.
  3. gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs: add the decal pass using the SAME additive pattern already used for fog volumes in this bead — a private `decals: Vec<PlacedDecal>` on SoftwareRenderer3D (both ctors are in that file, so zero external call sites change), `add_decal()`/`decals()` accessors, and an `apply_decal_pass(pixels, depth, w, h, decals, inv_proj, camera_transform)` sibling to `apply_fog_volume_pass`. Reconstruct the fragment world pos from depth (copy that reconstruction), then use the existing `Decal3D::sample_alpha(world_point, camera_distance) -> Option<f64>` to modulate albedo by `modulate`/`energy`. Wire at BOTH entry points.
  4. Tests: same shape as the new fog_volume_* tests (identity inv_proj + identity camera makes a fragment's world pos exactly its NDC, so expected values are hand-checkable).

I did NOT do steps 1-3: this lane is hook-blocked from the Rust builder, and declaring 709 never-compiled lines into gdserver3d — which gdrender3d, gdscene and everything above depend on — is precisely the blind cross-crate change that breaks the build for the whole swarm. It needs someone who can run the compiler.

STATUS: FogVolume half delivered (see previous comment). Decal half NOT started. Keep this bead OPEN; ideally split it, and add a separate bead for "declare + fix-compile the orphaned decal.rs into gdserver3d" since that is a real unit of work on its own.

title: Editor: Script mode shows a central script editor (currently the SCRIPT button is cosmetic; viewport stays 2D)
description:
Found via live browser inspection (localhost:8080/editor): clicking the SCRIPT main-screen mode button highlights it and opens the small bottom Script panel tab, but the CENTRAL view still shows the 2D viewport (grid + node markers). Godot's Script mode replaces the central area with a full script editor.

ROOT CAUSE (same class as pat-7i8u4 / pat-v4o3a): the frontend mode handler (editor_ui.rs setupModeButtons) for 'script' only POSTs the mode + clicks the bottom Script tab; it never swaps the central #viewport-panel for a script editor. The full script editor ALREADY EXISTS (renderScript/fetchScript/highlightGDScript/saveScript with header, line numbers, syntax highlight, auto-indent) but renders into the bottom #script-panel only. Server already exposes GET /api/script, /api/script/save, /api/script/main_view, and /api/editor/main_view returns component 'script_editor'/is_2d_viewport:false for script mode — but the frontend never renders a central script view.

SCOPE (phase 1): when editor mode is 'script', the central area shows the script editor full-size (relocate the existing #script-panel editor into a central container), not the 2D viewport; switching back to 2D/3D restores the viewport. Empty state offers a New Script action. Open-scripts list, find/replace UI, and breakpoint gutter wiring are follow-ups.

TEST (app-level): served /editor HTML has a central script-editor container and the mode handler shows it in script mode; GET /api/editor/main_view after POST /api/editor/mode {script} reports component script_editor / is_2d_viewport:false. (test: editor_script_mode_serves_script_editor_view)
acceptance_criteria: In script mode the central area shows the script editor (relocated from the bottom panel), not the 2D viewport; switching to 2D/3D restores the viewport. Served /editor HTML has a central script-editor container wired into the mode switch; GET /api/editor/main_view after POST mode script reports component script_editor / is_2d_viewport:false. Test: editor_script_mode_serves_script_editor_view

VERIFIED + CLOSING. Script mode now shows the script editor in the CENTRAL area instead of the 2D viewport. Implementation (editor_ui.rs): added a central #script-editor-panel + #script-main-host; new showScriptMode(on) relocates the existing #script-panel code editor into the central host in script mode and restores it + the viewport when leaving (reuses the full editor — header/Save/New, line numbers, syntax highlight, auto-indent — with no duplicate-id issues). Mode handler calls showScriptMode(mode==='script'). Test crates/gdeditor/tests/editor_script_view_test.rs::editor_script_mode_serves_script_editor_view PASSES (served HTML has the central container + wiring; /api/editor/main_view reports script_editor / is_2d_viewport:false). title: Verifier timeout kill misses sccache-parented rustc orphans
description:
The pat-regax process-group kill reaps the verify's bash/cargo/nextest tree on timeout, but compiles routed through RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache run as children of the long-lived sccache SERVER process (pid 1-parented), outside the verify's process group. Observed live 2026-07-14: after the platform_suite verify timed out and was group-killed, its rustc (gdrender3d) survived for 6+ min at 0 CPU, parented by sccache, holding an sccache slot.

Fix options: (a) on timeout, enumerate+kill rustc processes whose cmdline matches the verify's workspace AND whose start time falls within the verify window; (b) run verifies with RUSTC_WRAPPER unset and rely on the private target-verifier incremental cache; (c) sccache --stop-server on timeout (heavy: aborts other sessions' compiles).

Acceptance: a test in verifier.rs proving a wrapper-spawned grandchild outside the process group is reaped after timeout (analogous to verifier_timeout_kills_process_group).

title: Verifier: kill the entire process group on verify timeout (orphaned cargo-nextest survives and wedges the lane)
description:
Observed 2026-06-10: each 900s verify timeout killed the am-run/shell parent but left cargo-nextest alive as an orphan, each holding ~26 spawned test-binary children. Four generations piled up (15:48, 16:03, 16:18, 16:33 - exactly one per 15-min verify cycle), 102 hung child processes total, all stuck at _dyld_start (AMFI code-sign wedge). The orphans also held the cargo build-dir lock so every later verify spent its whole 900s waiting.

IMPLEMENTATION: in the orchestrator verifier lane, launch the verify command in its own process group (setsid/setpgid) and on timeout send SIGKILL to the negative pgid; then waitpid-reap. Also assert post-kill that no cargo-nextest/test-binary descendants survive (pgrep by pgid) and log if they do.

TEST: spawn a fake long-running command tree (sh -c 'sleep 1000 & sleep 1000') via the verifier timeout path with a 2s timeout and assert zero surviving descendants after the kill (test: verifier_timeout_kills_process_group).
close_reason: verifier.rs: bash verify child now leads its own process group (process_group(0)); on timeout SIGKILL the negative pgid (whole tree, not just bash) + surviving_group_members() post-kill assertion logs any orphans. Stops orphaned cargo-nextest from holding the build-dir lock. Test verifier_timeout_kills_process_group PASS (cargo nextest -p patina-orchestrator).

title: Editor viewport: node-name labels render as tofu/placeholder boxes for most glyphs (Player -> ??a???)
description:
Found via live browser inspection of examples/editor.rs (http://localhost:8080/editor, demo_2d.tscn).

REPRO: Load /editor with fixtures/scenes/demo_2d.tscn. The server-rendered viewport PNG (/api/viewport/png) draws each node's name label under its marker, but most characters render as empty placeholder boxes: 'Player' renders as five tofu boxes with only the 'a' glyph drawn. 'Enemy' and 'Ground' similar. Vertical ruler tick labels are also garbled.

ROOT CAUSE AREA: the editor overlay text path in the software renderer (gdrender2d / gdeditor viewport overlay) is drawing labels with a glyph set that covers only a small subset of ASCII (some lowercase letters work, most upper/lowercase missing). pat-04f (BitmapFont/FontFile text rendering) is closed, so either the overlay label path does not use that font system or the fallback atlas is incomplete.

IMPLEMENTATION: route editor viewport label drawing through the real font rendering path (full printable-ASCII coverage minimum) instead of the partial debug atlas; same for ruler tick labels.

TEST: render demo_2d.tscn editor frame and assert the glyph lookup used by viewport labels returns a non-placeholder glyph for every char in 'PlayerEnemyGround0123456789-' (unit), plus an app-level check that the rendered label bounding box for 'Player' is non-uniform across the 6 glyph cells (test: editor_viewport_label_glyph_coverage).
acceptance_criteria: Every char in 'PlayerEnemyGround0123456789-' resolves to a real glyph in the viewport label text path (no placeholder box); ruler tick labels legible; test editor_viewport_label_glyph_coverage passes

title: Editor: app-boot smoke test asserting each advertised surface is backed by a non-stub endpoint
description: One engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/editor_smoke_test.rs that boots the server, GET /editor, and asserts the DOM/endpoints for each advertised surface (3D viewport canvas, script main view, play controls, signals dock, asset browser) exist AND are backed by a non-stub endpoint. Catches the 'button in HTML, backend is a string flag' class. Tie its pass to a single top-level criterion editor-app-smoke-all-modes so the phase can't complete without it.
close_reason: Added engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/editor_smoke_test.rs with the editor_app_smoke_all_modes test (the editor-app-smoke-all-modes criterion). It boots the assembled EditorServerHandle, GETs /editor once, and for each advertised surface asserts BOTH that the surface's DOM marker is served AND that its backing endpoint returns real structured data (200 + a required JSON key present/non-null, non-empty where content is seeded) — catching the 'button in the HTML, backend is just a string flag' class of fake parity. Covers 11 surfaces: play controls (btn-play -> /api/runtime/status.running), 3D viewport (vp3d-toolbar -> /api/viewport/3d/state.yaw), script view (script-editor-panel -> /api/scene.nodes), signals dock (node-dock -> /api/scene.nodes), asset browser (assetlib-grid -> /api/assetlib/list.assets non-empty), profiler (profiler-panel -> /api/profiler.capturing), monitors (monitor-tree -> /api/monitors.monitors.'object/nodes'), debugger (debug-errors-list -> /api/debug/info.video_ram), animation (animation-panel -> /api/animations array), game toolbar (game-toolbar -> /api/runtime/status.time_scale), input map (pset-input-map -> /api/input_map.actions non-empty). Test PASS: every advertised surface is backed by a non-stub endpoint. Test-only change -> no regression. Source: validates the editor-parity work against its own advertised CAPABILITIES surfaces.

title: PBR mesh BRDF: port Godot's Burley diffuse + GGX specular to software shader + WGSL
description: Biggest remaining editor-viewport visual delta vs Godot: Patina shades meshes Lambert/Phong; Godot's scene shader uses Burley (or Lambert) diffuse + SchlickGGX specular with roughness/metallic. Port the default BRDF from servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/scene_forward_lights_inc.glsl (light_compute) into gdrender3d/src/shader.rs (software reference) AND SHADER_3D_WGSL in wgpu_pipeline.rs, keeping both byte-identical (extend render_3d_gpu_pipeline_test GPU-vs-software parity tests). Material3D already carries roughness/metallic.
close_reason: Burley diffuse + Schlick-GGX specular in gdrender3d shader.rs pbr_shade (Phong mode) and SHADER_3D_WGSL. Tests: burley_ggx_rough_metal_darker_than_smooth, d_ggx_peaks, phong_specular_highlight; gdrender3d lib 111 passed; GPU WGSL parse + shader_has_directional_shadow_hook_and_pbr.

title: Editor: undo/redo of node delete loses properties+children and breaks redo (stale id)
description:
Found via live API probing of undo/redo (16/17 ops correct; delete-redo failed). Two bugs in EditorCommand::RemoveNode (lib.rs):

1. REDO BROKEN: deleting node N then undo re-creates it under a FRESH arena id (the code comment even admitted 'the original NodeId cannot be reused'); redo's execute then removed the stale original id N -> 500 'not found: node N not found'. Reproduced live: Enemy id8 -> delete -> undo restores as id10 -> redo -> 500.
2. DATA LOSS ON UNDO: undo re-created a BARE node from only name+class via Node::new, dropping all properties (position, _script_path, etc.) AND the entire child subtree.

FIX: RemoveNode now captures the full subtree (name/class/properties/children, recursive CapturedNode) + sibling index on the first execute; undo restores the subtree exactly via restore_subtree and records the restored root id; redo (execute) removes restored_id when present instead of the stale original. Required making EditorCommand::undo take &mut self (symmetric with execute) and updating its 4 call sites + the Group case (iter_mut).

TEST: editor_undo_redo_test.rs::editor_delete_undo_redo_round_trips (app-level via EditorServerHandle): delete a Node2D with a position + child -> undo restores node, child, AND position -> redo removes again (200, not 500) -> undo restores again. PASSES.
acceptance_criteria: Deleting a node then undo restores it WITH its properties and child subtree; redo removes it again without error (no stale-id 500); repeatable. Test: editor_delete_undo_redo_round_trips

Full gdeditor lib suite 2008/2008 pass + the 4 undo integration bins pass + new editor_delete_undo_redo_round_trips passes. Fix: EditorCommand::RemoveNode captures the full subtree (CapturedNode: name/class/props/children) + sibling index on execute; undo restores it exactly via restore_subtree and records the restored id; redo removes restored_id instead of the stale original. Made EditorCommand::undo &mut self (symmetric with execute) + updated its call sites.

The two halves never met. Both hooks hand-rolled path resolution —
    let fs_path = path.strip_prefix("res://").unwrap_or(path);
— mapping res://bullet.tscn to the CWD-RELATIVE bullet.tscn, while SceneTree::change_scene_to_file

bullets/enemies is core to most games' — returned NULL unless the process happened to be running
from the project root. Nothing caught it because ZERO tests exercised .instantiate()/.new()
end-to-end anywhere in the tree.

res:// -> project root, user:// -> user root, plain/absolute -> PathBuf::from(path) (identical to the
old unwrap_or). Only delta: res:// with no configured root now yields null instead of silently
reading a CWD-relative file — matching the 'missing/unloadable -> null' contract both call sites
already document.

- engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/gdscript_preload_instantiate_spawns_live_scene.rs (NEW, 5 tests)

comments.text:
[IndigoBridge 2026-07-16] SCOPE + SUGGESTED SPLIT. This is a 4-feature pack; I delivered 1 of 4 (parallax). Recording the other 3 here because a PARTIAL on a pack like this gets auto-closed on compile, which would silently mark 3 real parity gaps as done. Each remaining item below is independently bead-able.

VERIFIED STATE (greps, 2026-07-16) — bead evidence is accurate:
- CanvasGroup .......... 0 hits anywhere. MISSING.
- BackBufferCopy ....... 0 hits anywhere. MISSING.
- ParallaxBackground ... 0 hits (before this change). MISSING.
- Parallax2D ........... only patina-runner/src/class_defaults.rs (defaults table, no impl).
- SCREEN_TEXTURE ....... exists ONLY as a shader-language token (gdserver2d/src/shader.rs) + editor autocomplete (gdeditor/src/shader_editor.rs, editor_ui.rs). Nothing captures a back buffer for it to sample.
- ViewportTexture ...... gdscene/src/sub_viewport.rs + class_db.rs registration; sub_viewport.rs has a CPU ColorBuffer (set_pixel/get_pixel/fill_rect/count_nonzero_pixels) but nothing binds it as a texture for a Sprite2D to draw.

DELIVERED HERE (1/4): Parallax2D/ParallaxBackground scroll + mirroring.
- gdserver2d/src/parallax.rs: ParallaxLayer gained `motion_mirroring` (Godot's euclidean-modulo wrap: `ofs -= den * floor(ofs/den)`, den = mirroring * scale) + `compute_offset_scaled(base_offset, scale)` mirroring Godot's `ParallaxLayer::set_base_offset_and_scale`. New `ParallaxBackground` (scroll_offset / scroll_base_offset / scroll_base_scale / scroll_ignore_camera_zoom) composes the base offset and drives layers, mirroring `ParallaxBackground::_update_scroll`.
- Defaults keep mirroring OFF, so all 4 pre-existing parallax tests are unchanged.
- Verify: scripts/rust_task.sh nextest run -p gdserver2d --lib parallax

STILL MISSING — suggested split into 3 beads:

1. CanvasGroup (group opacity composite). Godot composites a CanvasGroup's children into an offscreen buffer, then blends that buffer once with the group's modulate/self_modulate — so overlapping children do NOT double-darken at shared alpha. Needs a render-target detour in the 2D draw path. Home: gdrender2d (renderer.rs/draw.rs) + a CanvasGroup node in gdscene. Test: two overlapping half-alpha children under a CanvasGroup produce a uniform composite, vs. the doubled alpha you get without grouping.

2. BackBufferCopy + SCREEN_TEXTURE. BackBufferCopy(rect|screen) must copy the current canvas framebuffer into a back-buffer texture that a canvas_item shader samples as SCREEN_TEXTURE. The shader token already lexes (gdserver2d/src/shader.rs) but resolves to nothing. Home: gdrender2d framebuffer + gdserver2d shader binding. Test: draw A, BackBufferCopy, then draw B with a shader sampling SCREEN_TEXTURE and assert B's pixels carry A's colour.

3. ViewportTexture on a Sprite2D. Bind sub_viewport.rs's ColorBuffer as a sampleable texture so `Sprite2D.texture = ViewportTexture(path)` draws the SubViewport's rendered content. Home: gdscene/src/sub_viewport.rs -> gdrender2d/src/texture.rs. Test: render a distinctive colour into a SubViewport, draw a Sprite2D using its ViewportTexture, assert those pixels land in the parent frame.

LANE NOTE: gdserver2d and gdrender2d both have NO GPU dependency (gdcore/gdvariant/miniz_oxide/ab_glyph only) — this is CPU rasterizer work, so all 3 are testable with pixel assertions and do NOT need a GPU worker.

title: Editor viewport sky parity: sun disc + horizon haze (fog) missing vs Godot
description: Patina's procedural sky ignored directional lights (no sun disc/halo) and used pow(|y|,curve) gradients instead of Godot 4.6's mix(top,horizon,pow(1∓y,0.6/curve)), collapsing the bright horizon haze band. Ported the exact ProceduralSkyMaterial shader math (scene/resources/3d/sky_material.cpp) to both the CPU sampler (gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs) and the WGSL sky pass (wgpu_pipeline.rs): LIGHT0..3 sun discs with cos(sun_angle_max)/inv_sun_curve=1.6/pow(sun_curve,1.4) halo falloff, inv curves 0.6/curve, hemisphere-energy premultiply. Light3D gained angular_distance + sky (sky_mode) fields; editor preview sun now matches Godot's alt 60°/az 150° default, dim fill light excluded from sky. Tests: gdrender3d unit tests, gdeditor/tests/editor_sky_sun_fog_parity_test.rs (app-level), GPU↔CPU sun parity in render_3d_gpu_pipeline_test.rs. Verified live in Chrome at :8080.
